News.title: Teen who stabbed 16-year-old boy in heart at seaside town train station over £20 drug debt is convicted of murder
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FATAL STABBING Teen who stabbed 16-year-old boy in heart at seaside town train station over £20 drug debt is convicted of murder

A TEENAGER has been convicted of murdering a 16-year-old boy after repeatedly stabbing him in the heart over a £20 drug debt.

Joshua Ingram was brutally knifed twice during the horrific attack at Seaford Station, East Sussex, last September.



The murderer, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was convicted at Hove Crown Court today.

Jurors were told the 16-year-old was a “small-time drug dealer” who had supplied Joshua with drugs weeks prior, but had not been paid for them.



Sick Snapchat messages from the convicted killer were also read out in court.

One said: “Josh will perish if I don’t get my f money, that’s a fact and he knows this.

“I’m ready to sit in a prison cell for 30 years over a £20 sheet.”

The teen was on trial alongside two other boys, aged 17 and 15, accused of conspiracy to cause grievous bodily harm with intent.

Jurors found all three of them not guilty of that charge.

The 15-year-old was found guilty of assisting an offender, a charge that the 17-year-old had already admitted.

News.title: Horror moment pilot, 21, flies UNDER highway signage to make road landing after warning: ‘We’re not making the airport’
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a pilot narrowly misses highway signage to make a daring emergency landing on a major Florida road.

Flight instructor Emily Shelton, 21, performed the skilful manoeuvre after smelling fumes in the cockpit and warning air traffic control: “We’re not making it to the airport.”



Heart-stopping dashcam footage shows the moment she glided under highway signs, avoided traffic and safely landed on the interstate.

Emily, who has logged around 1,300 hours of flight time, had been taking a student on his first ever lesson when she reported the smell of burning fuel.



She told air traffic control: “Our oil pressure is dropping down into the red, and we do have fumes in the cockpit from the oil.”

As the situation worsened, she warned controllers that they would not make it to the airport.



She said: “We would like to go ahead and declare an emergency. We’re losing our engine.

“We are not making the airport; we are going down on I-10. We are lined up trying to avoid the cars.”

Controllers replied: “Roger. It’s at your discretion, safe spot as possible. We’ll get the vehicles out for you.”

Truck driver Eric Jordan, whose dashcam recorded the feat, described the landing as a “miracle”.



He told CNN affiliate WEAR: “If I wouldn’t have seen that shadow over my truck and slowed down, (the plane) would have been in the side of the cab.”

Escambia County cops rushed to the I-10 east in Pensacola where the plane touched down.

Emily said that she was reassuring the student pilot throughout the ordeal that she would find a safe place to land.



She told the outlet: “I feel my training has prepared me exceptionally well for this moment.

“I’ve practised this exact scenario many times, just never thought I’d actually have to execute it in real life.”

Nicole Gill, her boyfriend’s mum and a fellow pilot, told Fox: “It was such a near miss, and she did such an amazing job, keeping everybody safe.

“You realise how close and how dangerous it actually was.”

Nicole reflected on the moment Emily narrowly missed the highway sign.



She said: “Had she gone over it, she very well might have ended up in traffic versus that very small gap that she actually had to get over that truck but under the sign and also not overtake the cars in front of her.

“It’s just amazing that she was able to keep that plane under control.”

Nicole added that the 21-year-old is in good spirits after the ordeal.

She said: “She’s doing really well, and she’s ready to get back up there.”

Former army pilots have also praised the young flight instructor’s composure.



Tommy Lee, founder of nonprofit Pilots for Christ, told Fox: “The smoke gets in there, and you can’t breathe, so time is a critical factor on something like this.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“They did a great job getting it down quick.”

The US Federal Aviation Administration is investigating the incident.

News.title: Lifeguard ‘punched’ massive 12ft shark in English Channel before emergency beach closure with swimmers told to get out
News.content:
SLAMMERHEAD Lifeguard ‘punched’ massive 12ft shark in English Channel before emergency beach closure with swimmers told to get out

A LIFEGUARD reportedly punched a massive 12ft shark roaming close to the shore before panicked swimmers were told to get out of the water.

Coastguards shut off St Ouen’s Bay, on the northwestern tip of Jersey, at around 10.40am on Saturday following reports of a shark sighting.



RNLI lifeguard Tom Rolls said his colleague Nick bravely paddled out to the shark lurking just 40 metres off the coastline.

“He even said he kind of punched it as he was paddling, so it must have been really close to the surface,” said Tom.



“It was darkish grey, about 10 to 12 feet long, then it swam away really quickly from under his board.”

He added that the coastguards had been shocked to hear about the sighting, hoisting red flags and locking down the beach as a precaution.



While the species was not identified, onlookers were blown away by its size – around the length of two fully-grown adults.

Teenage surf instructor Jesse Heddercott, 16, was halfway through coaching when the order came through.



“Nothing like this has ever happened in Jersey before, so it’s pretty crazy,” he told the BBC.

“We thought it was just a tuna, or something, but then another lifeguard spotted it and it was confirmed to be – probably – a shark.

“They red-flagged the beach and we all had to get out.”

The shark reportedly swam south after a while, allowing coastguards to reopen the beach.

Richard Peirce, a wildlife campaigner with specialist knowledge on sharks, said he doubted the mystery creature was a Great White.



He told the Metro: “I haven’t seen a good picture of a dorsal fin that might have enabled me to have a stab at the species.

“It has to be a good picture because if you get a good enough side on a dorsal fin, it’s a bit like a human fingerprint.”

He said that a large dorsal fin would likely suggest it was a basking shark – although he couldn’t be certain.

Richard said: “Some people say the lifeguard who closed the beach acted hastily, but I don’t agree with that.

“I don’t know how crowded the beach was, but if there was a fin in the water and if that fin was going to cause people to worry, possibly even to panic, then it is going to be sensible to close the beach until the fin buzzed off.”



The UK is home to over 40 species of shark, including some of the fastest and most highly migratory on the planet.

The slow-moving basking shark tends to visit British coastal waters from April to October to feed on zooplankton blooms and are typically spotted around the south-west of England and west coast of Scotland.

It follows the discovery of a carcass belonging to the endangered smalltooth sand tiger shark on a beach in Jersey just months beforehand.

Described as an “elusive” and “deep-water species”, the species is typically found in warm and tropical oceans globally.

While there were 12 reported fatal shark attacks last year, humans are in turn responsible for the deaths of 100 million sharks, predominantly due to overfishing.



Richard said: “Sharks are under far more threat from humans than humans are ever likely to be from sharks.

“We are pushing some species, Great Whites amongst them, towards extinction.”

An RNLI spokesperson told the Metro: “RNLI lifeguards at St Ouens Bay responded to a suspected shark sighting off the coast on the morning of Saturday 1st August, by one of our Lifeguards in the water.

“A decision was made to red flag the beach and get all members of the public out of the water as a precaution.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The team then used a jet ski to survey the area, before concluding that there was no further sign.



“The beach was red flagged for 45 minutes. There have been no sightings since.”

News.title: Has the SpaceX rocket hit the moon? Why the Falcon 9 crashed – and what will happen next
News.content:
ALMOST four tonnes of SpaceX hardware has slammed into the lunar surface.

A disused Falcon 9 rocket stage, which spent over a year drifting through space, “completed” its accidental mission on Wednesday, August 5.



Has the SpaceX rocket hit the Moon?

The SpaceX rocket stage is expected to have hit the Moon at approximately 7.35am UK time on Wednesday, August 5.

Measuring roughly the size of a school bus, the empty upper stage will have crashed into the lunar surface at 5,400mph – more than seven times the speed of sound.



The collision is predicted to have occurred near the Einstein Crater, located on the far western edge (or “limb”) of the Moon.

Upon impact, the energy will have created a fresh crater estimated to be roughly 90 feet (27 metres) wide and kicked up a cloud of lunar dust which could reach heights of up to 60 miles.



Why did the Falcon 9 crash?

The rocket did not crash due to a system failure, computer glitch, or explosion.

Instead, it was simply abandoned space junk caught in a gravitational tug-of-war.

In January 2025, the Falcon 9 launched from Florida to send commercial robotic landers to the Moon – Firefly Aerospace’s Blue Ghost-1 and ispace’s Resilience.

While SpaceX famously recovers and reuses the bottom half (the first stage) of its rockets, the upper second stage is single-use.



Because sending cargo to the Moon requires large amounts of energy, the second stage used up all its remaining fuel during the burn, leaving no propellant to guide it back into Earth‘s atmosphere to safely burn up.

Left behind in a high-altitude orbit, the spent booster was left at the mercy of cosmic forces.

Over 18 months, gravitational pulls from the Sun, Earth, and Moon slowly pushed the rogue booster onto a collision path.

Can you see the crash site from Earth?

You cannot see the crash site or the impact with the naked eye or standard binoculars.

Even though the Moon is visible in the sky, a 90-foot crater is far too small to spot from 238,000 miles away without advanced scientific instruments.



The collision also took place near the Einstein Crater on the Moon’s far western limb, a region that is extremely difficult to observe clearly from Earth due to the Moon’s angle.

While professional observatories and astronomers with powerful telescopes may attempt to detect a faint dust plume lit by sunlight, standard backyard telescopes will not reveal the impact.

There was also no fiery explosion, as the Moon lacks an atmosphere or oxygen to support combustion.

As such, do not expect any images of the crash site to feature fire or smoke;.

Will video or photos of the crash be released?

Because there are no cameras stationed on the lunar surface, there was no live video of the crash.



But clear photographic evidence of the new crater will eventually be released to the public.

NASA and international space agencies are using lunar-orbiting satellites like NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and South Korea’s Danuri orbiter to track down the impact site.

NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), which circles the Moon, regularly maps the lunar terrain and will fly directly over the Einstein Crater region in the coming days.

Scientists will compare “before and after” satellite images to locate the fresh crater, measure its precise dimensions, and study the displaced soil.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

NASA typically processes and releases these high-resolution images within a few days to a couple of weeks following an orbital flyover, once the raw data has been downloaded and processed.



The findings will help researchers better understand lunar geology and assess the risks space debris poses to future Moon bases.

News.title: Scenic 2-mile English coastpath is CLOSED due to ‘public safety reasons’ as massive wildfire scorches 150 hectares
News.content:
A POPULAR coastal path has closed over safety fears following a major wildfire.

The scenic English walkway has banned public access for most of the month due to the hazardous conditions left by the blaze.



The King Charles III Coast Path in Dunwich was made unavailable from July 30 and will remain shut off until August 22.

The decision was made to close the trail after the wildfires on Dunwich Heath.



Fire crews were called to the Suffolk heathland on July 29 as the blaze rapidly spread across the coastal area.

Firefighters are now “focused on monitoring and extinguishing hotspots” and are using drones to identify any areas still alight.



The King Charles III path, which spans around two miles, has been closed off by Natural England due to “public safety reasons”.

Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Suffolk’s Fire and Rescue service said the danger is “far from over” following the “major incident”, due to the area’s scorching hot land.

Patches of the heathland are still at temperatures as high as 60C, with some parts much hotter beneath the surface.

“We want to make it clear that while the incident remains stable, the danger is far from over,” the Suffolk Fire and Rescue statement said.



“Firefighters are still dealing with hotspots across the site every day.

“What may look like ‘safe’, burnt ground can be hiding temperatures in excess of 60C at the surface, with temperatures significantly higher just a few inches below ground,” the spokesperson added.

“Underground tree roots, animal burrows and scorched earth continue to smoulder beneath the surface, creating hidden hazards that are not always visible from above.

“Please do not visit Dunwich Heath and do not enter closed areas. The landscape has changed dramatically as a result of the fire.

“Areas that were once familiar can now be difficult to navigate, making it easy to become disorientated.”

News.title: Russia confirms death of Putin commander’s son-in-law in Moscow restaurant blast…but is covering up IDs of other victims
News.content:
RUSSIA has confirmed the son-in-law of one of Vladimir Putin’s top commanders was killed in a restaurant blast in Moscow – but stopped short of revealing the identities of the other victims.

Daniil Peredriy, 27, died in the explosion during the lavish 55th birthday party of Russian Aerospace Forces commander-in-chief Alexander Chayko.



Chayko escaped the blast unhurt, but his 25-year-old daughter Maria reportedly suffered a “traumatic brain injury”.

Five others were killed in the explosion, but Russian authorities have yet to identify them.



It has fuelled growing speculation that several of the dead were senior figures from Putin’s military and intelligence services.

A Russian state database has now confirmed Peredriy’s death.

“One of his personal documents was declared invalid on August 1, the day of the terrorist attack at the Balzi Rossi restaurant,” the report said.

Former professional ice hockey player Peredriy married Chayko’s daughter in June last year.



The couple had organised the lavish £85,000 birthday celebration for her military father on Saturday.

The exclusive Balzi Rossi restaurant was packed with senior Kremlin insiders, high-ranking military officers, FSB agents and government officials.

A popular Telegram channel claimed: “The bomb, carried by a female suicide bomber, detonated as a vehicle with flashing lights approached the veranda.

“All the circumstances surrounding the identities of the event’s guests, the injured and the deceased are being carefully concealed.”



According to reports, the bomb was hidden inside a gift intended for Chayko.

The female courier may have been unaware she was carrying an explosive device capable of being detonated remotely.

Another 20 people were wounded in the blast, which rocked the foundations of the Stalin-era high-rise overlooking Moscow’s Kudrinskaya Square.

Chayko was appointed commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces in May 2026.



Ukraine has designated him a wanted “war criminal” over his alleged role in commanding Russian troops responsible for the 2022 Bucha massacre.

Russian forces under his command are accused of carrying out mass rapes, torture and executions in the town, just west of Kyiv, during the opening weeks of Putin’s full-scale invasion.

More than 450 civilians were killed in what is widely regarded as one of the worst atrocities of the war.

It comes as another senior Russian commander was reportedly killed by a Ukrainian FPV drone.

Major General Dmitry Mikhailov, 39, one of Putin’s youngest generals, is said to have suffered fatal injuries while travelling in an armoured Tigr vehicle.



He had allegedly ignored repeated warnings about the threat posed by Ukrainian drones before entering the combat zone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mikhailov has also been accused of war crimes during Russia‘s occupation of the Izium region, with Ukrainian investigators naming him among those responsible.

More than a dozen Russian generals have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

News.title: Body pulled from water in urgent search for boy, 13, who disappeared off coast after getting into difficulty
News.content:
SEA TRAGEDY Body pulled from water in urgent search for boy, 13, who disappeared off coast after getting into difficulty

A BODY has been pulled from the water amid an urgent search for a 13-year-old boy who disappeared after getting into difficulty.

The teen vanished off the coast of Hornsea, East Yorkshire, yesterday evening.



Police confirmed a body, believed to be that of the boy, was recovered from the water in the early hours this morning.

Official identification is yet to take place but the boy’s family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.



Emergency crews, including Yorkshire Ambulance and Humberside Fire and Rescue, were scrambled to the South Promenade at around 6pm.

Coastguard teams hovered over the choppy waters in a helicopter and scoured the sea in boats throughout the night.



Humberside Police taped off the beach and deployed special search teams, as well as high-tech drones, in a desperate search for the boy.

However, the force has now confirmed that their search has been called off after a body believed to be that of the boy was found.



Chief Superintendent Phil Booker said: “This is an incredibly heartbreaking outcome, and our thoughts are with the boy’s family and friends at this devastating time.

“Emergency services were called to the South Promenade in Hornsea shortly after 6pm yesterday following report of a concern for safety involving a 13-year-old boy who had got into difficulty whilst swimming in the water.

“An extensive search operation was launched involving specialist Humberside search officers including our Marine Unit and drone pilots, alongside HM Coastguard, Yorkshire Ambulance Service, and Humberside Fire and Rescue Service.

“Tragically, at around 4.30am this morning (Wednesday, 5 August), a body was recovered from the water.

“His death is not being treated as suspicious, and a file will now be prepared for the Coroner.



“We know the sadness and concern this will cause in the community, and we would ask that the family’s privacy is respected during this incredibly difficult time.

“I would like to thank all of the emergency services involved in the search, along with members of the public for their support and cooperation.”

It comes after a 14-year-old boy who drowned after vanishing in the River Thames was named as a “talented footballer”.

The boy, identified as Banta Sillah, died on Monday after disappearing in the water at Millwall outer dock in London.

Banta was described as a “talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week”.



A lengthy search operation was launched after Banta disappeared, involving rescue boats, police, fire crews and paramedics.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The frantic search of the Thames was concluded when the 14-year-old was recovered from the water at around 10pm.

He was sadly pronounced dead at the scene on Monday despite the best efforts of paramedics.

News.title: Solar Eclipse 2026 – where are the best places in the UK to witness the eclipse?
News.content:
BRITAIN is set to witness its biggest solar eclipse in over a quarter of a century.

On Wednesday, August 12, the Moon will pass in front of the Sun, plunging the UK into early-evening twilight.



It will be the most significant eclipse visible from British shores since the famous total eclipse of 1999, with up to 96% of the solar disc covered.

But because the event takes place in the early evening – peaking between 7pm and 7.15pm – planning where to stand is crucial.



The best places in the UK to witness the eclipse

The eclipse’s path of “totality” – where the Sun is 100% blocked – crosses Greenland, Iceland, and Spain.

While Britain misses out on complete darkness, western coastal areas will experience the deepest partial eclipse.



So, the further west and south-west you travel, the bigger and better the eclipse you will get.

The Isles of Scilly off the Cornish coast will see the largest coverage in Britain at 96.5%.

Land’s End in Cornwall comes in a close second at 95.8%, followed by Lizard Point at 95.6%.

Western Wales and Northern Ireland also get front-row seats.



Strumble Head in Pembrokeshire will reach around 94% coverage, while Belfast hits over 93%.

Eastern and northern regions will see slightly less coverage, though the views will remain spectacular.

London and Manchester will experience around 91.4% coverage, and Edinburgh 90.7%.

Even in the Shetland Islands, the far north-eastern tip of the UK, the Moon will still cover nearly 88% of the Sun.

The best places to spot the eclipse where you live

Obviously, heading west might not be a feasible plan.



But even if you’re in the eastern reaches of the UK, there are a number of steps you can take to make sure your view of the eclipse is unobscured.

Because peak eclipse occurs around 7.10pm, the Sun will be sitting low in the west-northwest sky, roughly 10 to 14 degrees above the horizon.

As such, street-level views in built-up areas may easily be blocked by houses, trees, or fences.

To secure the best vantage point near you, look for high ground or open spaces facing west-northwest.

Head to elevated local spots like your nearest hill ridge; getting above the tree line should give you an uninterrupted view across the landscape.



If you live in a town or city, seek out accessible high vantage points like rooftop bars, high residential balconies, multi-storey car parks, or office tower viewing platforms facing west, which can offer clear lines of sight above neighbouring roofs.

In more rural locations, west-facing beaches, coastal headlands, lake shores, and wide-open fields can offer flat, wide views all the way to the horizon.

How to view the eclipse safely

Looking directly at the Sun can cause permanent eye damage, even when 96% of it is covered.

Because totality does not occur anywhere in the UK, there is no moment during this event when it is safe to look at the Sun with the naked eye.



Regular sunglasses, no matter how dark or expensive they are, do not offer enough protection.

But solar eclipse glasses are completely safe, provided they meet official international safety standards.

Safe eclipse glasses must feature the official ISO 12312-2 code printed on the inside of the frame, which guarantees they filter out 99.999% of visible light, along with harmful ultraviolet (UV) and infrared radiation.

Only purchase glasses from recognised astronomy suppliers, science centres, or reputable opticians, and avoid unbranded, ultra-cheap pairs on online marketplaces, as counterfeit safety labels are common.



Check your glasses before use; if the lenses are scratched, creased, punctured, or coming away from the cardboard frame, throw them away.

Because the UK only sees a partial eclipse, your eclipse glasses must stay firmly over your eyes for every second you look directly at the Sun.

Other safe viewing options include:

Kitchen colanders: Hold a standard metal or plastic kitchen colander a few inches above a sheet of white paper with your back to the Sun. The holes act as pinhole lenses, projecting dozens of crescent-shaped shadows onto the paper below.

Hold a standard metal or plastic kitchen colander a few inches above a sheet of white paper with your back to the Sun. The holes act as pinhole lenses, projecting dozens of crescent-shaped shadows onto the paper below. Tree leaves: Nature provides its own projection screen. Stand under a leafy tree and look at the shadows cast on the pavement. The tiny gaps between leaves act as natural pinhole projectors, dotting the ground with mini crescent suns.

Nature provides its own projection screen. Stand under a leafy tree and look at the shadows cast on the pavement. The tiny gaps between leaves act as natural pinhole projectors, dotting the ground with mini crescent suns. Pinhole card projectors: Poke a small pinhole in a piece of cardboard. With your back turned to the Sun, let light pass through the hole onto a second piece of card held in front of you to safely watch the Moon move across the Sun.

If you plan to use binoculars, a telescope, or a camera, never look through them, even while wearing ordinary eclipse glasses.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The concentrated sunlight passed through lenses will melt the filter paper and cause instant eye damage.

You must buy purpose-built ISO-certified solar filters designed specifically to fit over the front objective lenses of your optical device.

News.title: 'I ditched my dream Italy holiday for a 'coolcation' - UK heatwaves changed me'
News.content:
'I ditched my dream Italy holiday for a 'coolcation' - UK heatwaves changed me'

EXCLUSIVE: Not wanting to risk the blazing temperatures of Sardinia, a heatwave fatigued mum wapped her dreamy Italian holiday for a milder 'coolcation', and has no regrets

View 7 Images Monica Krenner chose a 'coolcation' over a dreamy Italian getaway (Image: Monica Krenner)

A mum of one has shared how she swapped Mediterranean sun for a 'coolcation' and why she'll do it all over again next year.

‌



Monica Krenner and her husband, Peter, were on the brink of booking flights to Sardinia, Italy, on what was to be their young son Lewis's very first holiday.

‌



However, as the blistering heat took hold, the concerned parents didn't fancy braving the 39-degree scorcher with a three-year-old, and so had a last-minute change of heart. The fatigue of parenting during the relentless London heatwaves this summer meant she couldn't face more sweltering temps abroad.

‌



Monica, 57, tells the Mirror: "It was the best decision we made." Instead of dashing to the airport, the family made the five-and-a-half-hour journey from London to St Ives, Cornwall, back in June, where the relatively mild temperatures of between 16 and 24 degrees felt much more appealing.

7 View 7 Images The gentle breezes of St Ives, Cornwall, sounded much more appealing (Image: Monica Krenner) 7 View 7 Images The family enjoyed a 'perfect' holiday (Image: Monica Krenner)

‌



Explaining how she came to the decision, nutritionist Monica says that after speaking with a few friends, as well as some clients from Sardinia, she began to worry about just how hot the famously beautiful Italian island would get.

"After talking with a lot of people, searching all the weather apps, I then said, 'I cannot imagine going there, because then we have to be indoors the whole day, because it will be too hot to go outside'.

"And for the little one, the skin is very sensitive still. He's also not an amazing sleeper yet. Then I thought, 'Oh my God, if it's then hot on top because the weather, and he's not sleeping great, I'm already tired when I'm getting there, it won't be better when we stay somewhere where it's too hot this summer'."

‌



Once in Cornwall, Monica, Peter and Lewis were able to sleep comfortably at night after spending their waking hours walking in the fresh air and exploring the breathtaking Cornish coastline.

7 View 7 Images For little Lewis, it was his first time at the beach (Image: Monica Krenner) 7 View 7 Images Going forward, Monica is far more interested in exploring a destination 'rather than chasing guaranteed sunshine' (Image: Monica Krenner)

‌



It was little Lewis's very first time at the beach, and although Monica joked that "the seagulls didn't make it easy", it proved to be a very special, memorable trip.

Monica, who is originally from Vienna, Austria, says: "It was just relaxed, and in the evening, there was a nice breeze in your face. It felt like you could really breathe properly.

"We had a few drizzles, but even that was perfect. We had a very nice spacious room, so even if we didn't want to rush out, we could stay insideand have the windows open looking at the ocean. It was just lovely."

‌



Monica says that the trip "completely changed" how the family now consider their summer holidays. Going forward, they're far more interested in exploring a different options, "rather than chasing guaranteed sunshine."

Next year, the family intend to head off on another 'coolcation', and they are already planning their adventures. Currently, Monica and Peter are eyeing up trips to the coast of Denmark or Sweden, while bonny Scotland is also a top contender.

And the couple aren't the only ones looking for a crisp getaway. During the late June heatwave, Brits searches for cool-weather city breaks surged by as much as 33 percent compared to the previous week, according to online agent Opodo. Stockholm, Geneva and Gothenburg were the most coveted spots - world's away from sunny Spain or Italy.

‌



7 View 7 Images Monica and Peter are already planning their next coolcation (Image: Monica Krenner) 7 View 7 Images Mum Monica didn't want to have to worry about her son getting sunburnt (Image: Monica Krenner)

With four heatwaves in the UK already this summer, many holidaymakers are longing for gentle breezes rather than piercing sunbeams. So could it be that 'coolcations' are the new luxury in our climate change age?

‌



Ahead of the fast-approaching August Bank Holiday weekend, Airbnb has revealed that a number of UK destinations are seeing a surge in interest this summer, with bookings in Scarborough up by 30 per cent.

Picturesque Dumfries and Galloway in Scotland, which has seen bookings soar by 29 per cent, has emerged as one of this year's top 'coolcation' destinations, offering refreshing sea breezes and shady forest walks.

As for Monica, she's noticed this trend within her own social circles and reckons it makes perfect sense, especially for parents of young children looking for an easier trip.

‌



She explains: "People are looking for some cooler areas where they can breathe and enjoy being outside, not to cover up with 10,000 creams, and also with the little ones, not to cause them any sunburn."

The term sunny escape has taken on a whole different meaning in recent times. Awaze, the European holiday rental brand behind cottages.com and Hoseasons, found that searches for "escape the heat" rose by 300 per cent over the last three months alone. Online searches for 'coolcations', they say, were up by 420 per cent.

Matthew Price, Awaze's chief executive, notes that rising temperatures are "creating a new category of holidays", adding that they are "increasingly seeing holidaymakers look further afield to destinations known for their cooler climate, such as Scotland, Yorkshire and the northwest of England".

‌



Heti Morus, Marketing Executive at StayCotswold has also picked up on this trend, telling the Mirror: "It's no wonder 'coolcations' are growing in popularity here in the UK. I recently flew back from Bordeaux and saw the wildfires firsthand from the air.

"It just showed how quickly these situations can escalate, and it's made me think twice about flying to that part of France again anytime soon. Cooler staycation destinations are certainly looking even more appealing this year."

News.title: Strictly Come Dancing announces Graeme 'The Dogfather' Hall as 11th contestant
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing announces Graeme 'The Dogfather' Hall as 11th contestant

The latest Strictly Come Dancing contestant has been announced and will join EastEnders star Lacey Turner, pop singer Delta Goodrem and whole host of others in the star-studded lineup

View 2 Images Graeme 'The Dogfather' Hall will be on Strictly (Image: PA)

This Morning star Graeme 'The Dogfather' Hall has been announced as the eleventh contestant for Strictly Come Dancing.

‌



Bosses of the BBC Saturday night favourite have officially confirmed that Graeme, who is best known for providing advice about caring for dogs on ITV's morning show, is the latest celebrity to be gearing up to hit the dancefloor when all the action starts this September.

‌



In a statement, he said: "I can't believe I am joining the cast of Strictly for 2026. I have always loved dancing, so to have the opportunity to learn from the best in the business is a dream come true. I have watched the show for years, so to be a part of it feels like a very exciting challenge, albeit more than a bit nerve-wracking! I can't wait to get started. Bring it on!"

‌



View 2 Images Graeme works with dogs (Image: SWNS)

The news comes shortly after it was announced that football legend Shaun Wright-Phillips, who previously played for Manchester City and England, had also joined the star-studded lineup.

‌



"Dancing is in my blood—but mainly at family events!" said Shaun. "Strictly is definitely outside my comfort zone, but I’m super excited to get started and really looking forward to the challenge!"

Both of them will face competition from House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia who also joined the line-up this year. She said: "I can’t quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"

Prior to that, actress Jaime Winstone, who played Barbara Windsor in BBC biopic Babs before taking on the late actress' EastEnders alter-ego Peggy Mitchell in a flashback episode, is also taking to the dancefloor.

‌



She said: "I am so excited to announce that I will be joining the Strictly Come Dancing cast this year. I am no stranger to a dance floor, but the ballroom is a whole new world for me. I love a challenge though, so can’t wait to enter my showgirl era and get super sparkly!! Let’s get physical – see you on the dance floor!"

Paralympian Dame Sarah Storey, 48, has also been announced. The sports legend, who was born without her left hand, said she was excited, as she has "always loved watching Strictly". She also said she was doing it for her daughter Louisa, who "is a very talented dancer".

Presenter Will Best, who is best known for fronting Big Brother alongside former Strictly star AJ Odudu, called doing the show a "dream" after he was revealed to part of the line-up. “I’ve been lucky to do lots of live telly before, but absolutely nothing like this. And I cannot wait!" he added.

‌



“I have no idea if I can actually dance, but bring on the sequins, bring on the quicksteps, bring on the dance floor! I’m going to try to enjoy every minute of it.”

The other names announced include EastEnders star Lacey Turner, pop singer Delta Goodrem, Love Island winner Cach Mercer, Kim Kardashian's hairdresser Chris Appleton and Dani Dyer.

Fans of the programme will remember was supposed to take part last year, but after suffering an injury in rehearsals, she was replaced by West End star Amber Davies, so is making a comeback this time round. This year seems to be shaping up to be different than any other, as professional dancers Gorka Marquez Karen Hauer, Nadiya Bychkova, Michelle Tsiakkas and Luba Mushtuk have all parted ways with the show. Johannes Radebe, who was a pro dancer last year, has stayed with the show, but will take on a new role, as he has been announced as one of the presenters.
