News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr ‘REJECTS’ Real Madrid contract offer with Arsenal target ‘closer to a transfer than renewal’
Sports.content:
VINICIUS JR has reportedly turned down Real Madrid’s latest contract offer.

Los Blancos are said to have tabled an extension worth just over £360,000 a week.



But the Brazilian wants to be on a par with team-mate Kylian Mbappe, who picks up around £500,000 a week.

Arsenal are waiting to pounce on the first sign of opportunity if discussions between Vinicius and Bernabeu bosses collapse.



And according to Cadena SER, Vinicius is ‘closer to a transfer than a renewal’.

That is partly because he has less than a year left to run on his contract and does not want to screw Real Madrid over by leaving for free next summer.

And with tough negotiators in the Spanish capital unlikely to cave into his demands, ‘everything points to’ him edging towards the exit door, the report adds.

Mikel Arteta has made Vinicius his top attacking target as Arsenal look to build on last season’s Premier League triumph.

The 26-year-old has scored 128 goals in 376 games since arriving at the Bernabeu eight years ago.

Real’s £18.8m-a-year contract offer is equal to what Cristiano Ronaldo earned during his final few seasons at the club.

But with Mbappe only arriving two seasons ago, long-serving Vinicius feels he should be compensated on the same level as Madrid’s top earner.

The winger rocked up to training with his agent this week after an extended post-World Cup break.

Jose Mourinho, who was re-appointed in June, wants Vinicius to commit his future to the LaLiga giants.

And prising him away from Spain may not be easy for Arsenal, with Vinicius calling Real “the club of my dreams” where he wants to stay “for many years”.

Sports.title: ‘My toys’ – Cristiano Ronaldo shows off incredible £22m supercar collection including Ferraris and Bugatti
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO showed off his £22million supercar collection with an impressive Instagram post.

The 41-year-old took to social media to share three photos of himself standing in his garage surrounded by an array of stunnning cars.



The motors in the garage included two red Ferraris and a Bugatti.

Ronaldo has collected some incredible cars over the years, with models from the likes of McLaren, Mercedes and Lamborghini.

Sports.title: Why is Mo Salah wearing number 61 for Trabzonspor?
Sports.content:
MO SALAH has swapped England for Turkey, joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer!

Salah left Liverpool after nine years, leaving the club as the third highest scorer in their history.



The 34-year-old had his worst scoring season since 2015 last campaign, and left the Premier League as a free agent to find a new challenge.

That challenge is coming in Turkey, as Trabzonspor have signed the Egyptian winger as a free agent.



Salah almost guided Egypt into the World Cup quarter-finals against Argentina just weeks ago, so still has a lot to offer the Turkish side.

SunSport can reveal why Mo Salah is wearing number 61 for his new club.



Why is Mohamed Salah wearing number 61 for Trabzonspor?

Questions were asked when Mo Salah decided to switch from number 11 to 61, but there is a good reason for the change.

Salah is signing for Turkish side Trabzonspor, with the number 61 a historic symbol of the city he is joining.

61 is the province code in the Turkish vehicle registration plate system for Trabzon.

The number 61 has become a key symbol of the city and the club, it appears in shop names and across social media accounts, holding a special place in the hearts of supporters.



61 was worn most recently by Cihan Canak, with Yusuf Yazici, Abdulkadir Parmak and Baris Memis also among the names to have worn the number.

Ozan Tufan currently wears 11, and Salah is now a new symbol for the fans of Trabzonspor as number 61.

Sports.title: Max Dowman has chance to make Arsenal’s right wing his own with England stars away after rigorous fitness regime
Sports.content:
MAX DOWMAN has patiently been waiting in the wings for a chance to shine.

And the absence of Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for the start of Arsenal‘s pre-season is giving him the perfect opportunity to do so.



The England wingers are on holiday after their World Cup exploits – opening the door for 16-year-old academy sensation Dowman.

And on the evidence of last Saturday’s 4-1 pre-season win over Girona, he does not need a second invitation.



Starting out on the right wing, Dowman caught the eye with a goal and an assist.

Boss Mikel Arteta was delighted with his all-round game and he looks set to keep his place on Wednesday night when the Gunners face Real Betis in Dublin.



Dowman should then get another chance to shine in Sunday’s Emirates Cup clash with Borussia Dortmund.

But he may already be looking ahead to the Community Shield against Manchester City a week on Sunday and a Prem opener at home to Coventry five days later.

Madueke and Saka are not due back in training until next week, so Dowman has a chance to make the right flank his own.

That brings with it a certain pressure – but Arteta is confident the teen star can handle that spotlight.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Emirates chief said: “That’s what we want when you play for Arsenal. The expectations should be high and we should expect really good things. We know what he’s capable of doing.

“We now want him to be more consistent in terms of performance and the actions he can deliver.”

It is no coincidence Dowman looks ready to seize his pre-season chance as it is understood he worked on his fitness over the summer break.

Given he does not turn 17 until December, Dowman has not finished growing and Arsenal continue to carefully map out his training.

The winger trained with the first team when he was 14 but continued to play for the club’s youth sides.



Dowman alternated between the Under-18s and Under-21s, and that careful development continued last season as he was integrated into the first-team squad.

He played 153 minutes in the Prem and became the competition’s youngest scorer in March with his goal against Everton at 16 years and 73 days.

The sample size is small, yet the attacker showed in his cameos just why he is regarded as a top talent.



Per 90 minutes in the top flight last season, no Arsenal player created more chances from open play than Dowman.

The Gunners must be careful as they increase the teenager’s minutes but, mentally, he has coped incredibly well with such a rapid rise.

He has taken everything in his stride and continued to show the character traits from his time in the academy.

Arsenal U18s boss Adam Birchall had Dowman captain the side during the 2024-25 season – despite him playing three age groups up.

He, naturally, stood out and netted 15 goals in as many league games but his humility was noticeable, too.



After scoring a hat-trick in a 5-3 win over Leicester, Birchall recalls Dowman came into the dressing room and spoke about where the team – himself included – needed to improve.

He showed similar maturity when being targeted by defenders, who repeatedly tried to hack him down.

In one Uefa Youth League game two years ago, Sporting pinpointed Dowman and Arsenal U19s boss Max Porter made a point of raising it to match officials after the game.

The youngster, to his credit, stayed cool and there may be more rough treatment to come as Dowman’s star continues to rise.

But if there is one player he can turn to for advice, then it is Saka.



The winger was routinely roughed up at the start of his career and has been happy to mentor Dowman whenever he wants advice.

The same goes for skipper Martin Odegaard, who knows better than anyone what life as a teen star is like after joining Real Madrid at 16.

Declan Rice is another player that has been a big support to Dowman – publicly championing his talent and acting like a big brother.

Marli Salmon, 16, is closest to Dowman in the squad and another teenager tipped for great things.

Now, Arteta must manage the hype around Dowman, who has already appeared in an adidas advert with Gunners legend Ian Wright.



His sponsorship work beyond that, though, has been minimal and it underlines a desire to focus on performances on the pitch.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Adidas – like Arsenal – clearly see the teenager as a future star and his advert earlier this year came with the tagline…chaos or control?

Given what we have seen so far, Dowman can certainly bring chaos to a Gunners attack that has been built to control.

Sports.title: Bournemouth hammer Serie A rivals 10-1 in pre-season… before embarrassed side label it a ‘training session’
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH hit Genoa for double digits in a humiliating pre-season friendly.

But the Italian side has denied it ever happened – instead labelling it a ‘joint training session’.

This sparked angry responses from many Newell’s players, as their team-mate theatrically rolled across the turf.

Paredes has form for thumping the ball at his opponents.

During the 2022 he provoked a furious reaction from Virgil van Dijk after wellying the ball into the Dutch bench folllowing a hard challenge on Nathan Ake.

The contest went on to finish 2-2, with Boca star Alan Velasco grabbing a late equaliser.

Sports.title: Mo Salah seen in Trabzonspor shirt for first time as he’s mobbed after landing in Turkey ahead of shock transfer
Sports.content:
MOHAMED SALAH was seen in his new team’s colours for the first time since leaving Liverpool before he was mobbed by hundreds of adoring fans as he landed in Turkey.

The now-former Egyptian king of the Premier League agreed a deal to sign for Trabzonspor, which was announced on Tuesday.



But Salah, who departed Anfield at the end of last season as a free agent, has now been seen in the shirt of his new team for the first time.

Pictured while en route to Turkey in a plane, Salah was seen in the claret and blue colours of his new employers.



A club post on social media saw Salah doing some modelling with the kit, captioned: “Salah Mode: ON.”

Fans were loving the new look, which also confirmed he would wear the unorthodox shirt number of 61.

The 32-year-old also sent a message to his new fans in a short video posted by the club, once again from his flight.

He said: “Trabzon, are you ready?

“See you soon.”

The two-time Premier League winner has been enjoying his post-World Cup summer by spending some time in Mykonos, Greece.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But his new club announced the attacker was due to arrive in Istanbul on Wednesday before travelling to Trabzon, where he is set to sign a two-year deal by evening.

As for why he is wearing the No61 shirt for Trabzonspor, it is a way for him to connect with his new fans.

The number is an iconic number associated with the city, owing to it being the province code in the Turkish vehicle registration plate system.

Salah wore the number 11 shirt across his nine seasons at Anfield, and the two years before that with Roma.



He previously wore the number 74 at Fiorentina and had both 17 and 15 during his spell at Chelsea.

Meanwhile, at Basel he wore the number 22 shirt and at his first club, El Mokawloon SC, the number 31.

Salah had been courted by clubs in Saudi Arabia for years before sealing a surprise move to Turkey instead.

He will have a familiar face – relatively speaking – in the dressing room when he arrives in the form of Manchester United flop goalkeeper Andre Onana.



Salah scored in each of his last four games against Onana when he featured for Liverpool against their hated rivals.

Trabzonspor, who are seven-time Super Lig champions, are live streaming Salah’s arrival at the airport on their YouTube channel.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But hundreds of fans still turned out at the airport to welcome Salah to Turkey.



His new club last won the title in 2022, which was their first for almost 40 years.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan

Arsenal have agreed a deal with Newcastle United for Bruno Guimaraes and have their eyes set on their next summer signing

View 2 Images Arsenal are closing in on Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal have reportedly set their sights on a new central defender this summer as they look for cover after William Saliba aggravated a back injury on international duty at the World Cup. The Gunners are closing in on the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes and are exploring a blockbuster deal for Vinicius Junior, but a new defender is also being targeted.

‌



Saliba was replaced in France's semi-final defeat to Spain after going down injured, with new Chelsea signing Mazence Lacroix brought on as his replacement.

‌



Head coach Didier Deschamps did not risk Saliba during the third-placed play-off against England, though he did name the Arsenal defender on the substitutes' bench. Arsenal released a medical update four days later following Saliba's return to London from the United States.

‌



The club confirmed he is expected to miss part of the new season and will be sidelined for a prolonged spell as he undertakes a managed recovery programme. Now, according toFabrizio Romano, the Gunners will bring in a new defender to cover for Saliba.

Alan Brazil gives health update as radio legend returns to air after life-saving operation READ MORE :

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Deschamps revealed ahead of France's final game that Saliba had been managing the injury since March. He said: "William Saliba got injured, and it's problematic. He went through some examinations, and the injury did not worsen. He has faced that injury since March; he had some pain, and unfortunately, the pain was not bearable".

‌



Arsenal, however, maintain that thorough assessments have determined that surgery is not required. Specialist evaluations established that the injury would necessitate a period of rehabilitation instead.

Back troubles previously affected Saliba three years ago. His 2022/23 season was brought to an end prematurely after injuring his back during the second leg of Arsenal's Europa League last-16 encounter against Sporting.

He was sidelined for the final 11 Premier League matches and missed four of France's European Championship qualifiers as well. Saliba made his comeback four months afterwards during Arsenal's pre-season programme.

This summer, the former has featured as a right-sided centre half, partnering Gabriel against Girona, with boss Mikel Arteta evidently grooming him to deputise for Saliba.

Ben White represents another alternative who can shift infield from right-back to operate centrally. Arsenal, though, continue to monitor the market for cover.

England international Ezri Konsa was said to be under consideration, but Aston Villa's asking price in excess of £50m hampers any prospective transfer. Former Man City defender John Stones was also considered before joining Inter on a free transfer, while Arsenal have also been linked with other defenders.

Arsenal are on the brink of landing a statement signing regarding Guimaraes, after agreeing a £75m deal with Newcastle United for their captain.

The Gunners are also hopeful of pulling off one of the transfers of the summer by signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, who is in the final 12 months of his contract at the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher immediately rejects FIFA request after secret World Cup meeting
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher immediately rejects FIFA request after secret World Cup meeting

The former Liverpool captain has shed light on a private meeting he attended with FIFA officials and ex‑players to discuss proposals to play the World Cup every two years

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher says he was asked to support a new World Cup proposal (Image: YouTube / Football Ramble)

Jamie Carragher turned down FIFA's request to publicly support the idea of holding the World Cup every two years rather than the traditional four, following a secret meeting. The Sky Sports pundit revealed he had spoken with former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, now FIFA's chief of global football development, as well as a number of ex‑players about the proposed overhaul.

‌



This summer's tournament was staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, with European champions Spain lifting the trophy for the first time in 16 years. Luis de la Fuente's side beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal.

‌



The next World Cup is scheduled for 2030, with Morocco, Portugal and holders Spain set to jointly host the tournament. However, former Liverpool defender Carragher has revealed that discussions have already taken place about shifting the competition to a more regular cycle.

‌



Arsene Wenger forced to break silence on Gianni Infantino's disastrous World Cup plan READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

Speaking on the Football Ramble podcast, Carragher said he had taken part in discussions about the idea but didn't want to take it further. He admitted he was stunned when the organiser later messaged him asking him to publicly back the plan - a request he rejected immediately.

Carragher said: "I had a little chat with Arsene Wenger. He was getting involved with FIFA and it was all around this World Cup being every two years. He said, 'I'd like you to come on this other call with other ex players and we're going to chat about the ideas going forward'. I'm like, 'Brilliant, amazing'.

"We get on this Zoom and it wasn't just English players. It was like [Javier] Mascherano, there were foreign players from all over the world. They're basically talking about the pros of a World Cup every two years. I'm just listening, asking questions. I don't like the idea.

‌



"We finish this Zoom. I haven't said whether I don't like it or it shouldn't happen, I'm just chatting with these ex players. And the guy who was organising the Zoom, then text me and said, 'Okay, can you put this out?' - like supporting it. I was like, 'No, no, no'.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger is FIFA's chief of global football development (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Just because I came on the Zoom... I don't agree with and I don't want it. I think it's rubbish. This feeling of 'Once you're in here with us and you're on this Zoom, we're all these ex players and we're in.

"That was my insight into it with Wenger and Infantino above him, with getting all these ex players in and like, 'This makes us look okay'. Half of these ex players, they don't care. From that, I was like, 'I'm not having this at all'."

Plans for the proposal have not gathered momentum, though changes to the tournament were introduced for the first time this summer, with the 2026 edition expanding to 48 teams and adding an extra knockout round.

‌



Further reports suggest FIFA are considering pushing that even further, with a potential increase to 64 teams by the time the 2030 showpiece - the 100th anniversary of the World Cup arrives.

Both UEFA and CONCACAF oppose the idea, but CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez remains firmly in favour. The 2030 World Cup, co‑hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain, will also stage matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the centenary.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal, Newcastle and secret transfer battle both clubs are desperate to win
Sports.content:
There we have it then. Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal from Newcastle in a deal worth £75million.

It has become a familiar trend for the Magpies. Stand firm in the face of interest from their Premier League rivals, before ultimately sanctioning an agreement.

Guimaraes follows Alexander Isak and Sandro Tonali out of St James’ Park. A talent drain which has seen ambition move from conquering Europe to being able to qualify for it in the first place.

But as the dust settles on another transfer saga, the real battle begins in earnest. The PR war.

‌



It’s the battle every club is desperate to win. The battle played out in secret, with the victor usually declared on social media.

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

Winning favour with supporters after signing a player is easy, nobody has ever complained about receiving a shiny new toy. But for the selling club, it’s about softening the blow and explaining why they would have been silly not to do it in the first place.

Guimaraes to Arsenal is perhaps a perfect case study. After all, initial reports suggested Newcastle wanted £100m for their Brazilian talisman.

That’s the amount they received for Tonali, while Isak fetched a British record £125m a year ago. So the final figure is a huge win for the Gunners, whittling down £25m for a player Mikel Arteta was desperate to land.

‌



Arsenal will rightly suggest that in a market that has seen Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers go for more than £100m, getting Guimaraes for £75m in 2026 is quite frankly a bit of a bargain (in ridiculous Premier League terms).

Case closed then, Arsenal the winners, Newcastle the losers…cue gloating from the Gunners and meltdown from the Magpies. Or perhaps not so fast.

Because from the Newcastle side, this is unequivocally another transfer win. The Chronicle report that the Gunners opened negotiations with a frankly paltry offer of £45m.

‌



That wouldn’t even get you a Crysencio Summerville in a transfer window which has seemed to only veer from the ludicrous to the ridiculous.

Newcastle needed a bidding war to even get close to their valuation…or so they feared. Sources from Tyneside insist Arsenal were bidding against themselves, such was their desperation to land the midfielder.

In the end, Newcastle will boost their coffers to the tune of £75m, for a player - while still at the peak of his powers - will turn 29 in November.

View 2 Images Newcastle will receive £75m up-front for the Brazilian midfielder (Image: Shaun Botterill - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



And unlike so many modern transfers, it has been stressed this will be paid up-front, immediately giving the Toon a much needed cash-injection. And let’s not beat around the bush, they need that.

They need to change the narrative on a window which has seen key players AND Eddie Howe leave the club. They also need to provide prospective new boss Matthias Jaissle some funds to build the squad in his image - and that doesn't mean just doing what they've done so far, and signing potential. They need high-quality, Premier League ready performers for the here and now.

Arsenal felt they needed Guimaraes. A player that can help them retain their Premier League crown, while going one step further in Europe.

And so, who really won the saga? That will really depend on what you read, the same for every major deal this summer, as clubs scramble to shape the narrative in their direction.

‌



But this could be one of the great rarities in modern football. A transfer that probably suits both teams equally well.

Both sets of fans can shake hands and be on with their day then. That’s probably how it will work on social media…right?

Sports.title: Man Utd break silence on ticket controversy and admit causing 'significant distress'
Sports.content:
Man Utd break silence on ticket controversy and admit causing 'significant distress'

Manchester United have owned the fact their ticket investigation has caused distress to a number of fans, who thought they may lose their season tickets, with the club wanting to clamp down on touting

View 2 Images Man Utd have conceded that they made mistakes with their ticket investigation, which negatively impacted fans (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have admitted causing "distress" to fans by launching an investigation into how season ticket account details are used - leaving long-time and genuine supporters fearing they could lose their tickets.

‌



The Premier League giants began the process last month after they identified a number of accounts which they claim had activity which warranted further investigation.

‌



Red flags were raised when United clocked that, in one instance, 1,088 accounts had been accessed on a single device, according to the club, who have continued to defend their actions in private.

‌



But a host of genuine fans were left fearful that their season tickets would be confiscated without knowing the reasons and in a fans forum on July 30 those emotions were laid bare. United have now accepted they made mistakes in how they chose to execute their investigation.

Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint READ MORE :

The club said in a statement: "Manchester United accepts that the process may have caused distress for some loyal supporters, underestimated how common sharing account usernames and passwords was, and recognises that some fans may have felt they were being treated unfairly,"

"We recognise that many supporters have shared account login details in circumstances they regarded as legitimate, and we did not anticipate the extent to which this was occurring."

‌



United say a "satisfactory explanation" has been provided in a "substantial number of cases" with those individuals seeing any restrictions removed from their accounts.

View 2 Images Man Utd fans have expressed their anger with the treatment of long-term supporters

The club also believe the reasons for their investigation were valid amid a growing touting issue which, they say, deprives supporters of the opportunity to buy tickets. They have also maintained that any season tickets which are confiscated will be repurposed as season tickets - not sold as a corporate hospitality packages.

‌



United added: "There is no doubt at all this process has uncovered significant and organised touting which will enable us to remove tickets from touts and place them back in the hands of genuine fans. We believe this is something we are all aligned on."

The way in which United have treated their season ticket holders has come in for criticism. Last season, the club moved 500 season ticket holders from seats they had used for years in order to accommodate an increase in hospitality tickets.

Sports.title: Liverpool explore deal for PSG winger Mbaye

Liverpool have explored the conditions of a deal for Paris Saint-Germain's teenage winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

The 18-year-old, who predominantly plays off the right, is believed to be interested in moving to Anfield.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree fee for Guimaraes
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £75m fee with Newcastle for their captain Bruno Guimaraes.

He has been given permission to travel for a medical.

Guimaraes told Newcastle bosses earlier this summer that he wanted to join Arsenal if a suitable offer arrived.

Arsenal's opening bid was rejected but the 28-year-old now looks set to join the Premier League champions.

Guimaraes, who joined the Magpies in 2022 from Lyon for £40m, has made 195 appearances for Newcastle, scoring 31 goals.

Newcastle had been keen to ensure Guimaraes, who has two years left on his contract plus a club-held option for a third, cut if this deal goes through as expected, Newcastle will have made more than £240m from player sales this summer.

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona in a £69.3m deal, while Spurs signed Sandro Tonali for £100m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Bruno Guimaraes' best league goals for Newcastle

Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes

Sky Sports News understands Arsenal elongated the Guimaraes deal by refusing to contact Newcastle for weeks, which they found bizarre.

Agents were in between the clubs from the outset but Newcastle refused all pushes, which began with mentions of £40-£45m in June.

Newcastle didn't want to sell, and were desperate to keep Guimaraes. If their captain had said he wanted to stay, the club would have refused any offer from Arsenal or any other club. However, he has been very respectfully clear that he definitely wanted to go and this was his last big opportunity to win titles.

Attempts to persuade him otherwise and positive conversations were held, but Guimaraes was insistent he wanted to leave.

The deal could only happen if he said he wanted to leave and Newcastle would only deal at a fee which would become one of the highest ever paid in the world for a player over 28 years old.

Arsenal, via agents, continually said they wouldn't get anywhere near to such numbers so Newcastle continued to refuse to sell. Newcastle insisted it was their valuation, or no deal - and only if Bruno said he wanted to go. The player would only go on Newcastle's terms, similar to Tonali and Gordon.

In addition, a deal would only be sanctioned if the transfer was handled respectfully; for example, after he attended training camp in Spain, Newcastle feel Bruno has complied with this immaculately. They did not want a repeat of the Alexander Isak situation where he refused to train. Newcastle insisted there have been no fallouts and great respect remains between player and club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Catch up with the latest transfer stories from Sky Sports News including the news that Arsenal have a greed a fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes.

'Guimaraes move bad news for rest of league'

Sky Sports News reporter Chris Reidy:

"Arsenal's spine will now be ridiculous.

"Myles Lewis-Skelly was playing incredibly well at the end of last season and started the Champions League final. Martin Zubimendi is a World Cup winner and after some rest he will be ready to go. There's Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze in the No 10 position alongside the two potential starters in Declan Rice and Guimaraes.

"It's a world class midfield and if Arsenal weren't favourites for the title already, they are now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd thinks Bruno Guimaraes is an upgrade for Arsenal's midfield and will play alongside and fill in for Declan Rice.

"If they can add a left winger and some star quality in that position, which looks like the last piece of the puzzle, it looks like bad news for the rest of the Premier League.

"A few weeks ago, you'd have said this a fair fee but with the last few weeks we've had in the transfer window with some really high fees for midfielders, anything under £100m looks good value.

"Guimaraes is a little older but this is Arsenal's strategy, they want to win now. They have signed some younger players but last summer's deal to sign Viktor Gyokeres was to win now.

"Guimaraes won't need any time to settle in. He is one of the most consistent Premier League midfielders.

"Arsenal won't make money on him but he might get them closer to the Champions League and he might help them retain the Premier League. The Gunners aren't looking to the future, they want to win now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd says Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes would be the best partnership in the Premier League

It is easy to understand Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes.

The Newcastle captain is one of the Premier League's most complete midfielders, capable of dominating and destroying but also scoring and creating, with passing ability to match his physicality.

If the Gunners do secure his signature, he would be joining a group of midfielders which includes Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly. So where and how would he fit in?

Sports.title: Yokota targets 'special memories' as he seals Rangers move
Sports.content:
Rangers have completed the signing of winger Daisuke Yokota from Hannover 96.

The 26-year-old has moved to Ibrox for an initial fee of £2.75m plus add-ons, and has signed a three-year deal, with the option of an additional 12 months.

Yokota - who scored five goals and provided four assists in Germany's second division last season - could be included in Rangers' Europa League squad as they prepare to face Jagiellonia Białystok in the first leg of their third-round qualifier on Thursday.

He is Rangers' ninth summer signing, following Ivor Pandur, Vanja Dragojevic, Olwethu Makhanya, Ross McCrorie, Dan Neil, Lawrence Shankland, Cammy Devlin and Ben Godfrey.

Speaking after signing for the club, Yokota said: "I'm really excited to be joining Rangers. This is a massive club with a fantastic history, passionate supporters and high ambitions, so it's a proud moment for me.

"My aim is to help the team achieve success this season, and I hope we can create some special memories together. I'm looking forward to meeting my teammates, the staff and getting started."

Yokota's journey to Ibrox

Image: Yokota scored five goals and provided four assists last season

Starting his career in Tokyo, Yokota moved to Germany when he was 18 years old, first joining the academy of FSV Frankfurt and then FC Carl Zeiss Jena.

In 2021, he signed for Latvian club Valmiera and helped them win their first ever championship title in 2022 with eight goals and 10 assists that season.

Yokota spent a season in Poland with Górnik Zabrze before he joined Gent in 2024. He went on to have a successful loan spell at Hannover 96, before the deal was made permanent last season.

Manager Derek McInnes added: "We are really pleased to bring Daisuke to the club. He is a player we have been aware of for some time, and he brings qualities that we believe will really strengthen our attacking options.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Rangers started their Scottish Premiership campaign with a draw at Dundee United

"At 26, he has gained valuable experience across a number of different leagues in Europe. He is quick, direct and has the ability to make things happen in the final third.

"We are continuing to strengthen the squad in key areas, and I am looking forward to welcoming Daisuke to Rangers and working with him."

Sports.content:

"We ⁠know Carlos is doing everything he can to get back to playing tournaments as soon ‌as possible," Cincinnati Open tournament director Bob Moran said.

Sports.title: Chelsea set to clinch deal to sign Rayo Vallecano left-back Chavarria
Sports.content:
Chelsea are set to clinch a deal to sign Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria for a fee of around £16.3m (€19m) plus add-ons.

Both clubs are finalising the last details of the transfer. Negotiations between the two clubs have been ongoing for more than a month, with Chelsea identifying Chavarria as the replacement for Marc Cucurella following his move to Real Madrid.

At 28, Chavarría offers the experience Chelsea have been looking to add to their youthful squad this summer.

Image: Radar comparing Chelsea's Marc Cucurella and Rayo Vallecano's Pep Chavarria in the 2025/26 season

The full-back featured in 44 games in all competitions for Rayo Vallecano last season.

Chavarria started for Rayo Vallecano in last season's Conference League final, where they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace.

Rising up with Rayo Vallecano

Analysis by Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

It is perhaps telling that Andoni Iraola was in charge at Rayo when Chavarria was brought to the club in 2022. He is a coach who values players who can bring real intensity to a team's performance. Iraola loves his full-backs to overlap and Chavarria can do that.

He has since shown that he can do more than just get up and down the flank, becoming more comfortable underlapping or stepping into midfield, adding elements to his game. But that reputation as one of the hardest-working full-backs in LaLiga is what underpins it all.

Image: Chavarria competing with Lamine Yamal

Inigo Perez has helped bring more from Chavarria during their three seasons together at Rayo. The player naturally describes him as the best coach that he has worked with, allowing him to flourish as a modern full-back involved in all aspects of the team's play.

Stats that show what he can do

Analysis by Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

Chavarria was a key outlet for Rayo Vallecano last season, having over 2000 touches in LaLiga and supplying a stream of crosses from the wing.

Image: Crystal Palace's Daniel Munoz (left) and Rayo Vallecano's Pep Chavarria battle for the ball during the UEFA Conference League Final

Chavarria ranked among the top dozen players in the competition for crosses from open play and corners won. But it was a dual role for Rayo because he was also among the top dozen players for blocking crosses and winning possession in the defensive third.

Are we talking about a player with a wand of a left foot who can be Chelsea's creator in the way that Alex Grimaldo was for Xabi Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen out on the left? Probably not. But as a willing runner who stretches the play, his could still be an important role.

Sports.title: Silca Bay and Sea Suite face off as Brighton Festival begins
Sports.content:
Slica Bay, Sea Suite and Ben Nevis line up for the Brighton Mile this afternoon, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Silca Bay and Sea Suite feature among a field of nine for the Sapporo Japanese Premium Lager Brighton Mile Challenge Handicap on the opening day of the Festival of Racing at Brighton.

Sea Suite, twice a winner this year, has finished runner-up on his previous two starts and could continue to hold his form despite another 4lb rise in the weights. Ceren Fallon regains the ride for James Owen, whose team is on an upward trajectory at present.

Glen Nevis drops in grade, while course and distance victor Play Me warrants respect for Jim Boyle and Donagh Murphy. Having had a wind operation following two disappointing efforts since switching to Oli Rix, Here I Bow goes for top honours off a mark of 80.

6.40 Yarmouth - Dubai Charm and Dowman contest trappy nursery

Dubai Charm and Dowman contest a trappy edition of this Strawberry Fields Stud Nursery Handicap at Yarmouth.

Top weight Dubai Charm represents Richard Hughes and Neil Callan and looks to hold excellent claims. A dominant winner at this track and trip twenty-eight days ago, she looks capable of stepping up on that form and this daughter of Blackbeard might be tough to beat.

Dowman finished strongly when opening his account over this trip at Windsor back in June and has his first start having undergone a gelding operation. An opening mark of 73 looks fair and he can go well under Billy Loughnane, who is chasing winners as he attempts to land the jockeys' championship for the first time.

Beauty Box makes her handicap debut with a hood added, while Wait Geordie ran with credit in the Super Sprint Stakes at Newbury and cannot be ruled out.

Richard Spencer's Speed Of Sound has run two cracking races in defeat, finishing a close third on debut at Newmarket before chasing home Sorrengail in a warm event at Ascot. That form should be good enough to win a race, and he will be popular under Saffie Osborne.

Lady Of Hay made a pleasing debut when sixth at Newbury on racecourse debut last month and her trainer Andrew Balding reaches for a hood. A half-sister to the useful Anna Swan, she should be sharper for that initial experience and rates a big danger.

Babzini and Minkaas complete the shortlist, with the latter hampered when going well on her first start for TJ Kent last time out.

Best of the rest

Back at Brighton, recent winners It's Life and Buckland Belle clash in the Monty Bennetts 18th Birthday Handicap (4pm) before attention shifts Stateside to the Saratoga's Grade 1 A. P. Smithwick Memorial Handicap Hurdle (6.10pm). Fil Dor and McTigue line up here, alongside Roja Redemption.

Sports.title: Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane.

After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

When trailing 4-1, Draper sat down and spent the entire changeover crying, apparently uncontrollably.

The 24-year-old carried on and almost claimed a break before spiritedly holding serve one more time, before Atmane closed out victory in an hour and 52 minutes.

Draper had established himself as one of the biggest challengers to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's dominance of the men's game as he moved up to a career high No 4 ranking in June 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round match at the Canadian Open between Terence Atmane and Jack Draper.

It was around that time that Draper began suffering from a bone bruise in his left arm, an injury that has continued to hamper him ever since.

In 2026, he put together runs to the quarter-finals at Indian Wells in March and the semi-finals at Eastbourne in June, but has been unable to stay on the court consistently.

Sir Andy Murray has been part of Draper's coaching team since May, but Montreal was just the second tournament he has been able to play in during their partnership.

Draper has a wild card into next week's Cincinnati Open, but his defeat in Montreal is likely to raise fresh doubts over his participation there and at the US Open.
