World.title: Chad le Clos: ‘I lost 90% of my belongings in Sea Point fire’
World.content:
In a story of vastly conflicting emotions, Chad le Clos recently claimed a record 21st Commonwealth Games medal, but on the same night he achieved this feat, his Sea Point apartment was destroyed in a fire.

The 34-year-old won his 21st Commonwealth Games medal when South Africa took bronze in the men’s 4×100 metres medley relay last week, moving past the tally of Australian Emma McKeon.

However, he was then informed of a devastating fire that ripped through the apartment block in the Sea Point suburb of Cape Town, and led to the death of a 93-year-old man.



Chad le Clos reflects on loss and success

The famed swimmer admitted it had been a highly emotional time.

“I was doing the media scrum after ‘medal 21’, and one of the guys said he was sorry to hear about what happened back home and that my apartment building was on fire and that it was spreading like crazy,” he told KFM in an interview.

“That night was so significant to break that record… and so even though my apartment burnt down, I’m still truly grateful and blessed to have that record.”

After the Commonwealth Games, Le Clos said he had headed to Austin Texas to surprise his brother Jordan, and so he still had to pick up the pieces when he returned to Sea Point.

“My neighbour of nine years passed away in the fire, and I sleep with an eye mask and ear plugs, so if I was there who knows what would have happened. I think there were six or seven apartments burnt down, it was tragic … I’d say 90% of my stuff is all gone, the memorabilia alone is worth more than anything else… There is a lot of stuff I can’t replace…”

Swimming sensation pays tribute to neighbour

The Chad le Clos Foundation has launched a fundraising campaign to support residents affected by the fire.



“It has taken me a while to process this heartbreaking tragedy. On the evening of 30 July, amidst breaking the all-time Commonwealth record, a fire started in my apartment block, which quickly spread to my home. Sadly my home, where I’ve lived for more than a decade, burnt down and there is nothing left to salvage,” he wrote on Instagram.

“It is with a heavy heart that I extend my deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and friends of my neighbour of many years, who tragically lost his life in this fire.

“No words can truly ease a loss like this, but I hope the family knows that the thoughts of an entire community are with them.

“To my fellow neighbours whose homes and lives have been severely affected by this fire, please know that you are not alone. This is a tight-knit community and it is in moments like these that we lean on one another.”

World.title: eThekwini announces an 8-hour power outage on Thursday
World.content:
The eThekwini Municipality has announced a planned electricity supply interruption affecting the Plangweni Substation, scheduled for Thursday, 6 August, from 8:30 to 16:30.

The interruption is necessary to allow the City’s Electricity and Energy Directorate to continue commissioning a critical protection system as part of an ongoing substation upgrade project. Work of this nature typically requires supply to be cut so that technicians can safely test and configure the new protection equipment without risk to staff or infrastructure.

Multiple areas in eThekwini could be affected

Parts of several communities may experience disruptions, including Ebhodini, Emahlabathini, Eplangweni, Ezimbokodweni, Iziko Road, Kwahlongwane, Kwamakhutha, New City, Nqutshini Russia, Rhemia, Umbogintwini Industrial and Transnet Pipeline. Customers in these areas have been asked to make the necessary arrangements ahead of the outage.



The eThekwini municipality noted that not everyone in the listed areas will necessarily be affected. Residents who have not experienced a power cut by 9:00 can assume their supply will remain unaffected for the day, offering some households an early indication of whether they need to adjust their plans.

Safety reminder for residents

As with similar planned power interruptions, the public has been advised to treat all electrical installations as live throughout the outage period, since power could be restored without prior warning. This precaution is especially important for households that may attempt repairs or maintenance during the downtime, as the supply could return unexpectedly at any point before the scheduled end time.

Customers are encouraged to plan around the outage window, particularly those relying on electricity for work-from-home setups, medical equipment, or business operations in the affected areas. The municipality has not indicated any alternative arrangements for those significantly impacted, placing the responsibility on residents to prepare in advance.

No further details were given on when the normal supply would be fully restored beyond the stated 16:30 end time. However, customers are reminded that unplanned delays to commissioning work can occur.

World.title: Deputy President Paul Mashatile goes under the knife
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa says Deputy President Paul Mashatile will soon return to work after undergoing a minor surgical procedure. Image: Flickr

President Cyril Ramaphosa has expressed confidence that Deputy President Paul Mashatile will soon return to work after undergoing what the Presidency described as a minor surgical procedure.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Presidency said Ramaphosa visited Mashatile during his recovery and was pleased with his progress.

“The President visited the Deputy President on Tuesday afternoon and was assured he will soon be back at work,” the statement said.



Wide-ranging portfolio

Paul Mashatile has served as South Africa’s Deputy President since his appointment on 6 March 2023 and holds a wide-ranging portfolio across government.

As Leader of Government Business in Parliament, he is responsible for coordinating the executive’s legislative programme while also leading government’s efforts to accelerate land reform and agricultural support.

He has additionally been tasked with implementing rapid response interventions to address service delivery challenges, overseeing the rollout of the District Development Model to improve municipal performance, and coordinating initiatives aimed at resolving service delivery hotspots.



Heads peace missions

Paul Mashatile also leads South Africa’s response to HIV and AIDS as chairperson of the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC), serves as the country’s Special Envoy on South Sudan, and heads peace missions on the African continent when required.

His responsibilities further include chairing the National Human Resource Development Council, promoting social cohesion initiatives involving traditional and Khoi-San leaders as well as military veterans, and chairing the Cabinet committees on Governance, State Capacity and Institutional Development, and Justice, Crime Prevention and Security.

The Presidency did not disclose further details regarding the procedure or indicate when Mashatile is expected to resume his official duties, but said his recovery is progressing well.
