World.title: Hichilema unveils Copperbelt package, to personally pay ZESCO fees for 16,000 households
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has unveiled a sweeping package of economic interventions for the Copperbelt, promising to personally settle electricity connection fees for sixteen thousand households in Chambishi, revive mothballed mining operations and lower timber costs, as he pressed his case to voters in the province eight days before the general election.

Addressing campaign rallies in Mufulira, Lufwanyama, Kalulushi and Chambishi, the Head of State said his administration remained committed to accelerating economic recovery through investment in mining, energy, infrastructure and employment creation. He framed the announcements as a continuation of work already under way rather than new campaign promises manufactured for the occasion. Moreover, President Hichilemaa emphasized the importance of transparency in all government dealings.

In Chambishi, the President said he would meet the cost of connecting sixteen thousand households to the national grid out of his own pocket, rather than allowing the bill to fall on ZESCO. “I will talk to Zesco to connect 16,000 households in Kabaso area. I will deal with the connection charge also,” he said, reaffirming his commitment to reopening Chambishi Metals.

He directed local leaders to compile the names of eligible beneficiaries, stressing that only households on the approved list would qualify. “It means me, in my own personal business account, I will pay for these connections so that Zesco doesn’t go bankrupt. I want the names of these 16,000 beneficiaries and the cost of connection. I will take care of that,” the President said.

The commitment came alongside a disclosure that government had advanced discussions with potential investors interested in reopening Chambishi Metals, a move the President described as a major step toward restoring mining activity and creating jobs in the area. “I am working on the reopening of Chambishi Metals so that you can get jobs here,” he told residents.

Mining featured heavily throughout the Copperbelt tour. In Mufulira, the President pledged to engage mine owners directly on safety standards for small-scale miners and to facilitate the allocation of a mine dumpsite to young people seeking economic opportunities. “Bally is a responsible parent, so I want you to work safely and this is why I will engage the owners of the dumpsites,” he said.

He also disclosed that he had directed Mopani Copper Mines and pension fund managers to resolve outstanding pension issues affecting former mine workers, warning that he would personally intervene if no agreement was reached between the parties. The President further reaffirmed a commitment to reopening Chibuluma Mine’s Shafts Two and Seven, describing the move as an opportunity to create jobs similar to the revival of Shaft 28 in Luanshya.

“We are committed to revamping Shafts Two and Seven to create jobs for the youth and strengthen the economy,” he said. In Kalulushi, the President turned his attention to the timber industry, directing the Zambia Forestry and Forest Industries Corporation to review prices charged to local sawmillers, which he said had become prohibitively expensive.

“I have heard the concerns of sawmillers over the high cost of timber from ZAFFICO. I have engaged the corporation to ensure prices are within acceptable levels,” he said. The President also announced plans to formalise small-scale mining across the province by providing miners with legal and safe access to designated mining areas, a move intended to reduce the informal and often dangerous conditions under which many currently operate.

“We want legal mining. We want safe mining. There is no parent who sends his children to die every day in the pits,” he said, signalling a shift toward regulated artisanal mining zones rather than continued reliance on unregulated digging.

Beyond mining, the President announced that all volunteer nurses, doctors and teachers currently serving in Chambishi would be formally recruited into the public service, addressing a long-standing grievance among health and education workers who have provided services without full government employment status.

Additional pledges included facilitating construction of a modern bus station in Chambishi, expanding solar energy projects, improving radiology services at Chambishi Mine Hospital, and engaging stakeholders to resolve outstanding pension payments owed to former mine workers. The President urged residents to uphold peace and reject political violence, arguing that Zambia’s development agenda could only be sustained in a peaceful environment.

Beyond the Copperbelt-specific pledges, the President used the tour to defend broader elements of his economic record, including the government’s accumulation of foreign reserves, which he said had helped stabilise the Kwacha, support debt servicing and strengthen the country’s resilience to external shocks. He urged voters to reject what he described as a return to Patriotic Front-era governance, framing the Tonse Alliance as comprising leaders from the former administration.

The announcements landed in a province that has historically been a bellwether in Zambian politics, and where mining-sector fortunes are closely tied to household livelihoods. Whether the pledges translate into the promised connections and reopened shafts will likely become one of the more closely watched post-election accountability measures on the Copperbelt in the months ahead.

World.title: He Is Protecting His US$4 Million Eagle Milling Scandal by Spreading a False Narrative
World.content:
He Is Protecting His US$4 Million Eagle Milling Scandal by Spreading a False Narrative

By Augustine Mukoka

How can General Kanene hire cadres to virtually split his own medulla oblongata?

How can Garry Nkombo hire Bilden Shaloba and UPND thugs to block his own nomination filing and create mayhem at a funeral?

How can Brian Mundubile hire his own supporters to derail his campaign in Western Province?

How can Mundubile hire cadres to assault his own artists?

Surely, Mark Simuuwe must be a genius with vital information that could help the police unravel the situation.

Is Simuuwe confirming this is how the UPND sponsored the gassing of innocent citizens to get to power?

Simuuwe is a danger to Zambia’s democracy.

A senseless social media post by Mark Simuuwe in the wake of the chaos allegedly triggered by UPND cadres in Luampa, Western Province — as opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, arrived with their convoy yesterday — is not only contemptuous but also highly inflammatory. It represents one of the most irresponsible ways of handling a volatile situation during a highly charged and emotionally tense electoral period.

Rather than taking responsibility and addressing the chaos, Simuuwe, the ruling party’s Media Director, resorted to dogma in what appears to be a desperate attempt to win sympathy and shift blame onto the opposition. Such an attempt to insult the intelligence of any reasonable person is not only callous but deeply disturbing, particularly when it comes from someone who once sought parliamentary office but ultimately failed to secure it.

If you are unfamiliar with what I am referring to, here is Mark Simuuwe’s social media post made yesterday after Mundubile’s convoy came under attack and images of the assault on General Kanene circulated widely on social media.

Simuuwe wrote:

“PF is sponsoring their own cadres to wear UPND regalia, then cause chaos and attack either marketeers or their own members, then blame it on UPND.”They have also sponsored self-attacks in Southern, Western, Central, Lusaka, North-Western and Copperbelt so as to make it look like those are UPND strongholds where they are attacked, when in actual sense UPND is now nationwide.”You cannot manipulate voters in Eastern, Muchinga, Northern and Luapula using dirty politics.”We call upon citizens to be alert; their evil and dirty politics will never be clean — same old habits.”

How stupid!

His President later issued what many considered a feeble statement condemning the violence perpetrated by UPND cadres. In Kitwe, a bus linked to President Hakainde Hichilema’s operative — a Habasimbi — is a material of interest.

Widespread violence has previously been witnessed during the UPND’s own intra-party adoption process. It has occurred in Kaputa among UPND cadres, been witnessed in Magoye, and also recorded in Bweengwa, Choma and Monze — all involving UPND members. In Mazabuka, violence has likewise occurred between rival UPND factions: those supporting independent candidate Garry Nkombo and those backing President Hichilema.

Yesterday, that violence extended, as in parts of North-Western Province, beyond internal UPND disputes and targeted opposition leader Mundubile. In typical UPND fashion, blame is once again directed at the opposition. How are Zambians expected to accept such claims with Mark “Eagle Milling” Simuuwe at the centre of this narrative?

Simuuwe may convince UPND supporters and those willing to believe him unquestioningly, but he cannot deceive everyone all the time. He may believe he is clever today, but even the President’s chief political messenger cannot remain convincing indefinitely.

The Zambia Police should investigate Simuuwe’s statements and determine whether any laws have been broken by the publication of information that could inflame public tensions or misrepresent events. His public assertions deserve careful scrutiny alongside any investigation into the violence itself.

The continued violence suggests that those responsible have little regard for peace or democratic principles. The President’s restrained response has done little to reassure the nation that there is sufficient political will to decisively confront political violence.

This is why Simuuwe must be stopped from spreading a false and misleading narrative of events. Zambia deserves peace. Zambia deserves a free, fair and credible election.

Stop the violence. Stop spreading false narratives. Take responsibility and ensure that all political actors are held accountable so that the country can move forward peacefully. It’s disgusting to watch Zambian elections degenerate into a bloodbath.

Arrest Simuuwe. Stop the chaos.

Editor’s Note: The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this publication. This is an opinion/column piece.

World.title: General Kanene hospitalised after machete attack at rally
World.content:
Musician hacked as poll violence spreads across three provinces

Musician Clifford Dimba, popularly known as General Kanene, remains admitted at the University Teaching Hospital after suspected ruling party cadres attacked him with a machete during a campaign rally in Shibuyunji District on Monday, one of several violent incidents that have rattled Zambia’s election campaign with polling day approaching.

The musician was performing at a rally for independent parliamentary aspirant Ibrahim Mwamba in Mwembeshi East Constituency when armed men arrived in a Toyota Land Cruiser and disrupted the gathering. Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said preliminary investigations showed the attackers assaulted Dimba, inflicting a cut to his head, before turning on property at the scene.

“They allegedly assaulted Dimba, inflicting a cut to his head and damaged a Mitsubishi Triton registration number BAZ 5004 belonging to Mwamba,” Chilabi said. He added that the assailants also made off with an HP ProBook laptop, two mobile phones and sixteen thousand kwacha in cash, the value of the remaining damaged property still being assessed.

Dimba was first taken to Chawama Level I Hospital before being issued a medical report at Westwood Police Station and later referred to the University Teaching Hospital, where he remains under treatment. Police dismissed circulating social media rumours that the musician had died, and confirmed that a machete recovered at the scene had been retained as an exhibit.

Chilabi said dockets have been opened for aggravated robbery, unlawful wounding and malicious damage to property. “This matter is being treated as a serious criminal offence, and all those involved will be identified, arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the laws of Zambia,” he said. The rally had also been addressed by independent council chairperson candidate Mutumba Denise.

Mwamba’s own campaign team was not spared. According to reports carried in the aftermath of the attack, the aspiring MP suffered a fractured knee and ankle during the same disturbance, while campaign equipment including public address systems was stolen or destroyed.

The Shibuyunji attack came in the same week that supporters of the United Party for National Development and the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity clashed in Luampa District, Western Province. Suspected UPND supporters attempted to block the campaign convoy of NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile, resulting in stone-throwing between the two groups before the confrontation was brought under control.

President Hakainde Hichilema condemned both incidents in a statement posted on his Facebook page, warning that political violence would not be tolerated regardless of who was responsible. “Let it be clear that violence, intimidation or lawlessness by any political party, candidate or supporter will not be tolerated,” the Head of State said, describing the reports as deeply concerning and deserving the strongest condemnation.

The President stressed that every political party had a lawful right to campaign during the period allocated by the Electoral Commission of Zambia, and warned that anyone found disrupting that process would face the consequences. “Anyone who attempts to disrupt or prevent that process is breaking the law and must face the full consequences,” he said, calling on parties and their supporters to conduct campaigns peacefully and within the confines of the law.

In a twist that has complicated the picture, the UPND media team issued its own statement alleging that elements of the former Patriotic Front, operating under the NRPUP banner, had orchestrated a scheme to sponsor individuals to wear UPND regalia, stage violent incidents and falsely implicate the ruling party. The party said the operation involved deploying people dressed in UPND attire to provoke violence against marketeers, members of the public and, in some cases, even their own supporters, before circulating claims that UPND members were responsible.

According to the statement, similar operations were alleged to have been planned or carried out in Southern, Western, Central, Lusaka, North-Western and Copperbelt provinces, with the stated aim of creating an impression that the ruling party was losing support in its traditional strongholds while manipulating public opinion in Eastern, Muchinga, Northern and Luapula provinces. The UPND called on law enforcement agencies to investigate any credible reports of individuals impersonating its members or engaging in criminal conduct while falsely associating themselves with the governing party.

NRPUP figures have pushed back against suggestions that the party or its sympathisers are behind coordinated violence. Former Shiwang’andu MP Stephen Kampyongo, commenting separately on unrelated editorial criticism of his party, argued that it was unfair to characterise NRPUP’s campaign in purely negative terms, though he did not address the Shibuyunji attack directly.

Civil society voices have urged all sides to allow police investigations to run their course rather than trade accusations. Commentary published this week argued that words of condemnation from political leaders, however sincere, are no longer sufficient on their own, and that the true test lies in whether suspects are identified, arrested and brought before the courts without delay or selective treatment.

With the national vote now just over a week away, the Electoral Commission of Zambia and the police have both faced renewed calls to demonstrate that campaign-period rules are being enforced evenly. Officials from both major parties have said they expect law enforcement to treat all reported incidents with equal seriousness, regardless of which side is implicated, as the country enters its final stretch before Zambians go to the polls.

World.title: Copper  Queens dare Malawi at WAFCON  ‎ ‎
World.content:
The Copper Queens are confident ahead of Wednesday night’s decisive Group C match against Malawi at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Rabat.

‎

‎Kick off is 22h00 at Al Madina Stadium. Zambia must beat Group C leaders Malawi to advance to the quarterfinals, while Malawi will only need a draw to finish top of the group.

‎

‎Zambia opened the tournament with a 6-0 win over Egypt before a 1-0 loss to Nigeria.

‎

‎Coach Nora Häuptle said the team’s quarter-final destiny remains in their own hands and the squad is approaching the game with positivity.

‎

‎“We are in a good position, all in our hands. For me, it’s a privilege to be in this situation. To play the last game in this group and to be in the situation where it’s in our hands. We don’t need to rely on other results but what we face; that’s not pressure,” Häuptle said.

‎

‎The Swiss trainer said Zambia will focus on performance rather than qualification permutations.

‎

‎“We don’t go out and calculate tomorrow on the pitch. We go out and focus on our performance, as always. We have a clear approach to how we want to face Malawi. I think we played three very good halftimes out of the last four, and we want to build on this stable approach,” Häuptle said.

‎

‎She predicted a tough match, noting both teams are evenly matched and know each other well.

‎

‎“Tactic-wise, there are not so many secrets, I would say, in this game, but again, we bounce back to us,”_ she added.

‎

‎Goalkeeper Hazel Nali said the team is ready for the challenge.

‎

‎“We know exactly what we want and we know exactly what’s on the table. Our main focus is to work extra hard because football is played on the pitch. What we want as a team is to fight and give our all for the country.”

‎

‎Nali said the team is working on containing Malawi’s speed and is not dwelling on past results.

‎

‎The top four semi-finalists at WAFCON will qualify automatically for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

Zambia is aiming to better its 2022 bronze medal won under the late coach Bruce Mwape.

World.title: Mporokoso Praises ECZ Ballot Handling Professionalism
World.content:
Political stakeholders in Mporokoso District have commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for the professional manner in which they have handled the receipt and offloading of ballot papers ahead of the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

The stakeholders say the Commission has demonstrated transparency and professionalism by addressing concerns raised by political party representatives throughout the process.

They explained that although the ballot papers for Mporokoso Constituency arrived at 21:50 hours on August 3, 2026, the ECZ remained professional in advising that they could not be offloaded at night in line with the Commission’s guidelines, a decision that was unanimously accepted by all stakeholders.

And the United Party for National Development (UPND) representative Patrick Mulenga praised the Commission for adhering to established procedures, describing the level of professionalism exhibited by ECZ officials as commendable.

Meanwhile, National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) representative Chrispine Kachusha expressed satisfaction with the manner in which the process was conducted, stating that the Commission met the expectations of all stakeholders through a transparent and orderly exercise.

The ballot papers were successfully offloaded today, August 4, 2026, at 07:50 hours in the presence of political party representatives and other election stakeholders.

The ballot papers arrived in Mporokoso District yesterday in preparation for the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

World.title: Five Lusaka Residents Jailed Five Years for Possession of Pangolin
World.content:
The Lusaka Magistrates Court has sentenced five people to five years imprisonment each with hard labour for illegal possession of a live ground pangolin.

Handing down judgment on 28th July, 2026, Magistrate Mutinta Mwenya convicted Lutangu Namushi, 35, Melody Mwangala, 39, Abigail Sitali, 22, and Nawa Pelekelo, 33, after a full trial.

Peter Mukela, 32, had earlier changed his plea to guilty on 15th May, 2026 and was also sentenced to five years with hard labour.

According to the Department of National Parks and Wildlife (DNPW) the five were arrested on 1st February, 2026 at Novare Mall in Lusaka during an intelligence-led operation where officers found them in possession of a live ground pangolin weighing about seven kilograms.

Investigations established that the pangolin was sourced from Kalabo District in Western Province and transported to Lusaka where it was allegedly intended for sale to foreign buyers.

All five were initially charged with illegal possession of a protected species under the Zambia Wildlife Act.

DNPW has described the successful prosecution as evidence that intelligence-led operations are working to disrupt wildlife trafficking networks.

“Pangolins are protected under the Zambia Wildlife Act and are among the most heavily trafficked mammals globally due to demand for their scales and meat,” DNPW stated.

“Removing them from the wild not only threatens the survival of the species but also undermines the health of ecosystems in which they play an essential role, DNPW said.

The Department urged members of the public to help protect pangolins by refusing to buy, sell or keep them, and to report any suspicious activity to the nearest police station or DNPW office.

The conviction comes as Government and conservation partners intensify efforts to combat wildlife trafficking and safeguard Zambia’s biodiversity for tourism and ecosystem health.

World.title: President Hichilema Orders Jobs for Mufulira Volunteers
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has directed that all volunteer nurses and teachers in Mufulira District be employed.

Speaking during a community engagement meeting in Mufulira District, President Hichilema instructed the United Party for National Development (UPND) aspiring Members of Parliament candidates to compile a list of the names of volunteers for employment.

The President reiterated his commitment to continue creating more jobs for youths, highlighting that in the last four years, his government has employed 45,000 teachers,20,000 health workers and many more officers in the army, Zambia National Service,and Police.

“I Hakainde Hichilema,umubomfi wenu (your servant) have made a decision that all volunteer teachers and nurses will be employed, “the President said.

“God works through people and today He has used me to employ you,” Mr Hichilema added.

Meanwhile, the President urged Mufulira residents to vote for the UPND in order to enable them complete the various infrastructural projects being undertaken in the district.

“Vote for us so that we complete the Mufulira-Ndola Road, Mufulira-Mokambo Road, Kamuchanga Modern Market, and the Mufulira District Hospital,” Mr Hichilema said.

He stated that once re-elected, the UPND will continue with the social cash transfer programme, the cash for work Programme and the free education.

“In the Patriotic Front government children were failing to go to school due to lack of school fees, but due to our free education policy,2.5 million children have gone back to school, “he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Hichilema said he wants youths to conduct mining activities safely and legally.

Mr Hichilema said he is in the process of facilitating for youths to legally and safely mine at dump sites urging them to be patient and desist from illegal mining activities.

“No responsible parent would want their children to go and mine in where they can die, Bally is a responsible parent and I want youths to mine safely, no guns and no violence, “the President said.

President Hichilema said his government will also embark on the construction of Township Roads in Mufulira.

Meanwhile former Copperbelt Minister, Elisha Matambo highlighted some of the achievements of the New Dawn government.

Mr Matambo said the UPND government has constructed 6 level one hospitals, and also commenced construction of Mufulira District Hospital which had stalled for several years.

“Hospitals had no equipment and no drugs but under our government we bought equipment and medicines are now available,” he said.

Mr Matambo said the UPND have made several scores including resuscitating Mopani Copper Mine and Konkola Copper mine, the Free Education and building up of government reserves.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 5, 2026
World.content:
Tinubu Approves Up to 80% Pay Rise for Nigerian Troops

President Bola Tinubu has approved a salary increase of between 30% and 80% for about 250,000 members of Nigeria's Armed Forces, effective from 1 September. The move is expected to increase the military's annual wage bill by N264 billion, from N660 billion to N924 billion. Junior soldiers, from private to staff sergeant, will receive the highest increase of 80%, while personnel from colonel to warrant officer will get 50%, and senior officers above colonel will receive 30%. The government said the pay rise is part of broader efforts to improve troop welfare and strengthen military operations as security forces continue to combat insurgency, banditry and kidnapping across the country. Tinubu said the increase recognises the sacrifices of military personnel and reaffirmed his administration's commitment to equipping the armed forces with the resources needed to tackle Nigeria's security challenges.

Eight Years On, Zimbabwe Yet to Deliver Justice for 2018 Victims



Eight years after Zimbabwe's security forces killed six people and injured 35 during the 1 August 2018 post-election protests, no one has been held accountable, according to Human Rights Watch. The rights group said President Emmerson Mnangagwa has failed to implement key recommendations of the Motlanthe Commission of Inquiry, despite initially pledging that those responsible would face justice. Human Rights Watch said no security personnel have been arrested or prosecuted, victims have not been compensated, and the lack of accountability has fuelled further abuses, including the deadly crackdown on January 2019 protests. The organisation urged Zimbabwean authorities to implement the commission's recommendations and end what it described as a cycle of impunity and human rights violations.

Funerals Held After Ethiopia Monastery Landslide Kills 14

Funerals have been held for some of the 14 people killed after a landslide struck the Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St Mary Monastery in Ethiopia's Amhara region during an overnight prayer service. The hillside collapsed after hours of heavy rain, burying worshippers gathered for a holy water cleansing ritual. Seven others were injured, five seriously. Rescue efforts have now ended, with 11 victims buried at the monastery and others returned to their hometowns. Landslides are a recurring hazard during Ethiopia's rainy season. Scientists have warned that climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall across East Africa.

Pesticide Poisoning Suspected in Deaths of 15 Kenya Elephants

The deaths of 15 elephants outside Kenya's Amboseli National Park have sparked concern. The Kenya Wildlife Service said preliminary findings suggest they may have been poisoned by cyanide-containing pesticides used on nearby tomato farms. Wildlife officials found traces of cyanide in samples from some elephants and said the animals showed signs consistent with poisoning. Investigations are continuing, and deliberate poisoning has not been ruled out. Conservationists and local farmers have questioned the pesticide theory. They said that elephants would have had to consume large quantities and that other wildlife sharing the same habitat was unaffected. The incident has also renewed concerns over illegal agrochemicals, weak enforcement of pesticide regulations and growing human-wildlife conflict as farming expands into elephant migration corridors.

Close 

Cameroon's Biya Makes Military Changes From Geneva

Cameroon President Paul Biya, 93, has reshuffled the country's military while remaining in Geneva, Switzerland. He has been in Geneva for nearly two months on what his office describes as a private visit. In the signed decrees, Biya appointed officials to key military posts and promoted five colonels to brigadier general, including the reappointment of Raymond Jean Charles Beko'o Abondo as head of the elite presidential guard. The move comes amid growing speculation over Biya's health and prolonged absence. Critics have warned of an institutional vacuum; however, the government insists he remains in charge and will return to Cameroon soon.

World.title: South Africa: Govt Vows to Intensify Health Corruption Fight - South African News Briefs - August 5, 2026
World.content:
South Africa Vows to Intensify Health Sector Anti-Corruption Drive

President Cyril Ramaphosa has said that the fight against corruption in South Africa's health sector is far from over, despite progress in recovering stolen public funds and prosecuting suspects, reports EWN. Speaking at the opening of the R1.6 billion King Nyabela Hospital in Mpumalanga, Ramaphosa also revealed that plans to build 11 new public hospitals are now before the National Treasury as government explores innovative ways to fund the projects. Ramaphosa said rooting out corruption will remain central to the government’s efforts to strengthen the public health system and restore public confidence in State healthcare.

Madlanga Inquiry Resumes Corruption Probe



The Madlanga Commission of Inquiry is set to resume its hearings, continuing its examination of the Investigative Directorate Against Corruption's handling of the fraud and corruption case, reports SABC News. The commission has been examining the investigation and prosecution of Crime Intelligence Head Dumisani Khumalo and six other officials from the unit. The inquiry is expected to hear from a new witness as it scrutinises the investigation, evidence assessment and legal processes that led to the arrests.

Impeachment Committee Appeals Ruling Halting Ramaphosa Inquiry

South Africa's Parliamentary Impeachment Committee has joined an application to appeal directly to the Constitutional Court against a Western Cape High Court ruling that temporarily halted its inquiry into allegations of misconduct against President Cyril Ramaphosa, reports EWN. The committee argues the judgment undermines Parliament's constitutional oversight role and accountability, saying the interdict has far-reaching implications for the separation of powers.

Africa grows more than half of the world's finest long-staple cotton. It earns less than three percent of what that cotton is eventually worth. This is not a trade problem. It is a narrative problem — and allAfrica is setting out to fix it.

There is a number that explains much of what is wrong with how the world finances Africa. It is not a trade figure or a debt ratio. It is an annual cost — up to $4.2 billion — the amount by which negative media stereotypes inflate African sovereign borrowing costs every single year. The story the world reads about Africa costs Africa, concretely, in higher interest rates and slower capital flows.

Cotton to Cloth is the moment we unlock the full power of the infrastructure we have built over the years.



"The gap between raw commodity and finished product is not a production gap. It is a perception gap — and journalism, data, and storytelling can close it." — Amadou Mahtar Ba · Co-Founder, allAfrica Global Media

The story begins in the field. West African cotton is among the finest on earth — long-staple, clean, commanding a premium on international markets. It leaves the continent as raw fibre. It returns as finished garments at twenty, thirty, sometimes fifty times the price. The countries that grow the raw material that clothes the world are rarely named as manufacturers. That is the gap this initiative addresses, one story at a time.

World.title: Mozambique: Government Concerned At New Wave of Fuel Shortage
World.content:
Maputo — The Mozambican government has expressed its concern at the new wave of fuel shortage in several parts of the country, following the crisis that affected the country last April and May.

The previous fuel shortage caused long queues of vehicles at filling stations in Maputo and other cities. According to the authorities, the crisis was influenced by the US-Israel aggression war against Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which is responsible for the daily flow of almost 20 percent of the world's oil sales.

About 80 per cent of Mozambique's fuel imports pass through routes connected to the Strait of Hormuz, which means that the impact of the war in the Middle East is potentially disastrous for the country's economy.

This situation forced the government to increase, at the beginning of this May, the prices of the main liquid fuels by up to 45, 5 percent.

The authorities also pointed out the bankruptcy of fuel distributors and the shortage of foreign currency (particularly US dollars) as the main cause of the crisis.

The wave of fuel shortage has returned. According to government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration, Inocêncio Impissa, speaking to reporters on Tuesday after a meeting of the Council of Ministers (cabinet), the government is assessing the causes of the new crisis.

"We are still assessing the situation to understand what is actually happening, so that we can solve the problem. The government is gathering information to find the causes of the problem so that something must be done", he said.

World.title: Africa: Africans Bear the Brunt of Biodiversity Loss
World.content:
For millions across Africa and the developing world, the biodiversity crisis is not an abstract problem - it's the soil that no longer yields bountiful harvests and the fish that no longer return to coastal waters.

But the world spends 30 times more money destroying nature than protecting it, and Africa often lacks the necessary resources to address the crisis, the head of the UN's Biodiversity Convention warned this week at a major scientific forum in Nairobi.

Biodiversity refers to the variety of life on Earth. In addition to maintaining natural ecosystems, having a variety of species - both flora and fauna - also supports human survival through food and medicine.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Thanks to biodiversity, we have food. Biodiversity gives us clean water. It helps us fight climate change. It makes us more resilient," Executive Secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity Astrid Schomaker told UN News. "All these issues matter to all of us."

Africa is home to 25 per cent of the world's biodiversity but has also lost about 24 per cent of its species since the pre-industrial period, according to a recent study.

The continent is uniquely impacted by biodiversity loss because many people rely on its bountiful natural resources to earn a living.

Ms. Schomaker said climate change is the single biggest driver, and Africa is especially vulnerable to climate shocks.

But because of massive government subsidies for fossil fuels and private industrial spending around the world, biodiversity loss outpaces efforts to protect it, UN Environment Programme, UNEP, warned earlier this year.

Ms. Schomaker said rising temperatures, invasive species, pollution and overexploitation of land and water all deplete the resources rural and coastal communities rely on for food, income and clean water.

From science to funding

If the recent meeting of the UN's Subsidiary Body on Scientific, Technical and Technological Advice identified biodiversity loss as a problem, the Subsidiary Body on Implementation - meeting until 12 August in Nairobi - will focus on how to solve it.

Negotiators are now working through how to embed biodiversity into national decision-making, draw financial institutions into the conversation and raise the money needed to close the gap.

"We have a very solid understanding of where we are," Ms. Schomaker said. "And now it is taking this understanding of where we are and translating it into recommendations on how we can move forward faster."

© UN Nairobi Astrid Schomaker, Executive Secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), addresses the seventh meeting of the Subsidiary Body on Implementation (SBI-7). Cautious optimism ahead of COP17

Despite alarming figures, reports submitted to UNEP by 125 countries show strong global engagement on solving the crisis of diversity loss.

Close 

In fact, whether it be planting a tree, creating insect havens or avoiding harmful chemicals, UNEP says everyone has a role to play in protecting biodiversity.

The recommendations from the two Nairobi conventions will inform Member States' negotiations and decisions at COP17, the biennial meeting of parties to the Biodiversity Convention, which begins on 19 October.

This year in Yerevan, Armenia, countries will review progress toward the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted at COP15 as a roadmap to reverse biodiversity loss and help people live in better harmony with nature.

"That is our biggest challenge: How can we turn this around?" Ms. Schomaker said. "How can we make everybody understand that biodiversity matters for them - that destroying biodiversity means you essentially destroy what you are building your lives on, and then make the right decisions."

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Approves Up to 80% Salary Increase for Nigerian Soldiers
World.content:
Junior soldiers, who make up much of the military's frontline fighting force, received the largest percentage increase, suggesting the government is directing the biggest pay improvements to personnel most actively engaged in combat operations.

President Bola Tinubu has approved a salary increase of between 30 and 80 per cent for members of Nigeria's Armed Forces, a move expected to raise the federal government's annual military wage bill by N264 billion as the country continues to battle terrorism, banditry and kidnapping.

This was disclosed in a Tuesday statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga who noted that the pay review will take effect from 1 September.



The presidency said about 250,000 personnel would benefit from the salary review. While it did not explain the figure, it likely refers to active members of the Nigerian Armed Forces currently on the federal payroll across the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force.

The military's total strength is not officially disclosed, although public estimates have Nigeria's active military strength at about 230,000 personnel.

Percentage increase by rank

Under the new salary structure, officers above the rank of colonel--including brigadier generals, major generals, lieutenant generals and generals--will receive a 30 per cent salary increase.

Personnel from colonel to warrant officer will receive a 50 per cent increase, while soldiers from private to staff sergeant will receive the highest adjustment of 80 per cent.

The presidency said the revised package would increase the armed forces' annual salary bill from N660 billion to N924 billion, representing an additional N264 billion in personnel expenditure.

The increase amounts to an overall rise of 40 per cent in the military wage bill, although the actual increase for individual personnel varies by rank.

Junior soldiers, who make up much of the military's frontline fighting force, received the largest percentage increase, suggesting the government is directing the biggest pay improvements to personnel most actively engaged in combat operations.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that troops fighting across the country's frontlines have lamented about poor welfare.

While the presidency has yet to release the revised salary table, Defence Minister Christopher Musa had earlier said the minimum monthly salary for the lowest-ranked soldier was increased from N49,000 to N100,000 under the Tinubu administration. It is not immediately clear whether that increase forms part of the newly approved salary review or was implemented separately. The presidency has also not disclosed the new salary figures that will result from the latest adjustment, which takes effect on 1 September.

The announcement comes as Nigerian troops remain deployed in sustained counter-insurgency and internal security operations across the country, including the North-east, North-west and North-central, where they continue to confront Boko Haram, ISWAP, armed bandit groups and kidnappers.

The salary adjustment also forms part of the Tinubu administration's broader efforts to improve troop welfare alongside investments in military equipment, weapons procurement and technology aimed at strengthening operational effectiveness.

Announcing the decision, Mr Onanuga explained that President Tinubu said members of the armed forces deserved greater support in recognition of their sacrifices.

"The men and women who help to keep us safe in our homes must be supported and appreciated in the course of their duties to our nation," Mr Tinubu was quoted as saying.

Close 

The president said his administration would continue to prioritise troop welfare while modernising the armed forces with the weapons and technological tools required to confront security threats.

"Our administration believes that no nation can achieve greatness without security. We therefore remain resolute in mobilising all military and law enforcement assets to eliminate security threats and protect the lives and property of all Nigerians," he added.

Mr Tinubu urged military personnel to regard the salary increase as a demonstration of the government's appreciation for their service, expressing confidence that the armed forces would prevail against groups threatening the country's security.

World.title: Zimbabwe: U.S. Disputes Zimbabwean Govt's Recent Account On $365 Million Health Deal
World.content:
THE United States Embassy in Harare has disputed recent claims by Information Minister Zhemu Soda on the US$365 million health deal Zimbabwe rejected late last year.

Zhemu told Parliament that the US government sought to collect private health data for medical research which they were not sure would benefit Zimbabweans.

"As the Government, we felt we could not put the lives of our people at risk because we did not know the intention," said Soda.

According to a US Embassy spokesperson who spoke to NewZimbabwe.com this does not make sense as Zimbabwe has benefited from America's medical research through treatment and vaccines for decades.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The US government through PEPFAR has spearheaded Zimbabwe's fight against HIV/Aids by providing most of the country's ARVs and condoms.

"We reject the recent mischaracterisation of the terms of the Health Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) made by a high-level Government of Zimbabwe official, which described the MOU as a threat when, in fact, it would have provided $365 million in lifesaving assistance over five years for Zimbabwean health programs, including HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, maternal and child health, laboratories, and outbreak response," said th US Embassy spokesperson.

"The MOU required very reasonable conditions: that the Zimbabwean government co-invest, assuring sustainability of the programs; provide financial accountability and transparency to guarantee funds benefit the people and communities of Zimbabwe; and share specimens when outbreaks occur, which is a long-standing global practice to quickly develop solutions.

"Assertions that the United States was seeking personal/private data of Zimbabweans are categorically false. Any suggestion that Zimbabweans would not have benefitted from American medical research is disproven by decades of U.S. assistance, through which Zimbabweans have received US treatments and vaccines."

The same programme has been successfully presented to 34 countries with a total of US$14.3 billion in health funding.

World.title: Uganda: Opposition Politician Tortured, Faces Abusive Charges
World.content:
Nairobi — Investigate Ill-Treatment Allegations; Drop Charges

The Ugandan authorities have brought abusive criminal charges against an opposition politician, Muwanga Kivumbi, apparently based on his criticism of the president's son, who is head of the armed forces, Human Rights Watch said today.

On July 29, 2026, the authorities charged Kivumbi, a deputy president of the National Unity Platform (NUP) Uganda's main opposition party, with "inciting violence" and "managing an unlawful society," after unlawfully detaining him for 19 days in an unrevealed location the day after he was released on bail for separate politically related charges. Kivumbi is one of several government critics that the military has in recent weeks arbitrarily seized, held incommunicado, and handed over to courts for abusive prosecutions.



"Ugandan authorities are weaponizing the justice system to harass and target its critics and opposition," said Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. "The government needs to end these malicious prosecutions, and instead ensure accountability for the numerous rights abuses and scaling up of human rights violations in the country."

On July 10, armed plainclothes and uniformed soldiers dragged him from his car at a police roadblock and drove off with him to an unrevealed location. On the morning of July 19, the soldiers left him at a police station in Kampala, media reported.

The police took him 66 kilometers away to a magistrate's court in Butambala later that day, where they brought new charges against him. Based on the charge sheet, Kivumbi's charges arise from a speech he made to his supporters at a public gathering in Butambala on the day of his initial release.

The authorities did not specify the basis for the charges in the charge sheet. But in a video of this speech, seen by Human Rights Watch, Kivumbi criticized President Museveni's son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the chief of the Uganda Peoples' Defence Force, for engaging in politics as a military officer.

During the July 29 court hearing, Kivumbi said that the security officers who abducted him blindfolded him and took him to a location he could not identify, where they held him for days in a small room, and kicked and beat him until he bled from his head. A witness who saw Kivumbi upon his release told Human Rights Watch that he had scars on his head, arms, legs, and back, apparently from the beatings.

The authorities had initially arrested Kivumbi on January 22, alongside scores of other National Unity Platform supporters around Uganda's contested general elections on January 15, holding him until he was released on bail in July. Kivumbi had been running for a parliamentary seat during the elections which he lost.

The authorities who arrested Kivumbi in January accused him of orchestrating "a violent attack on Kibibi Police Station and Butambala Electoral Commission Tally Centre," and causing "serious damage to sections of the Butambala-Gomba road" and multiple vehicles that "directly resulted into the deaths of seven people" on the days before and after election day. Kivumbi had rejected the allegation, saying security forces had raided his home on election day and shot and killed several members of his campaign team who were there.

The Agora Centre for Research, a Ugandan organization, reported that the armed forces killed at least seven people at Kivumbi's home, including election officials, who had run into a garage for safety during the raid.

The Ugandan authorities should urgently and impartially investigate the circumstances of those killings and hold the those responsible to account, Human Rights Watch said.

Although Uganda's Constitution guarantees the right to bail and prohibits arbitrary arrests and detention, security agencies frequently re-arrest people after courts have granted them bail, and courts have denied bail to other political opponents, extending their pretrial detention beyond maximum periods under Ugandan and international law.

In another such case, on July 29, a former presidential candidate, Kizza Besigye, who is on trial for treason and has been imprisoned since November 2024, collapsed during a court hearing and was hospitalized. The courts have previously denied him bail, despite requests by his family to have him released to allow him to receive private medical treatment.

On July 15, soldiers seized and unlawfully detained one of Besigye's lawyers, Elias Lukwago, then sent him to pretrial detention on treason-related charges. The authorities later deported another of Besigye's lawyers, Martha Karua, to Kenya on July 22. On July 30, the High Court denied Lukwago bail, which he had sought to receive medical treatment.

Close 

International human rights law requires any pretrial restrictions on criminal suspects to be consistent with the right to liberty, the presumption of innocence, and the right to equality under the law. The UN Human Rights Committee, the international body that provides authoritative analysis of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, has stated that pretrial detention imposed on suspects as punishment, among other reasons, is inconsistent with those rights.

Ugandan law criminalizes torture under the Prevention and Prohibition of Torture Act 2012, and the Human Rights (Enforcement) Act 2019 provides for personal liability for public officers who commit human rights violations.

"Kivumbi's charges are only the latest in Uganda's intensifying clampdown on critics of the government," Budoo-Scholtz said. "The authorities should drop all criminal charges against him and ensure that all security officials implicated in his ill-treatment and enforced disappearance are held to account."

World.title: Century-old Italian ice recipe is creating childhood memories for a whole new generation
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

What started in 1915 as a neighborhood Italian ice shop without a sign is ready to expand nationwide by offering franchises.

"It was one of those, 'If you know, you know. It's that little green shack,'" DiCosmo's Italian Ice owner Eileen O'Connor told Fox News Digital of the original Elizabeth, New Jersey, location.

Now a community institution in Metuchen, New Jersey, DiCosmo's is hoping like-minded businesspeople will carry on their tradition by opening Italian ice shops in other places, with particular interest in franchises along the Eastern Seaboard and in warm-weather states, where shops can stay open longer.

$20 FROZEN YOGURT? PROTEIN-PACKED DESSERT CRAZE HAS CUSTOMERS LINING UP

O'Connor's great-grandparents emigrated from Italy and settled in New Jersey.

"The story goes that it was a particularly hot summer, and my grandmother was looking for something similar to the granita she had had in Italy," O'Connor said. "She wanted something refreshing."

Granita is an icy dessert made with water, sugar and flavorings, such as lemon, coffee or almond. It's popular in Sicily, where it's commonly eaten for breakfast with a sweet, warm brioche bun.

The DiCosmo family had a little corner store in Elizabeth. It was there, O'Connor said, that her great-grandmother came up with a recipe to recreate the granita she missed using the fruits available at the local market, which happened to be lemon, the traditional flavor in Italy.

The original recipe, a hand-squeezed and hand-churned mixture of fruit, water and sugar, hasn't changed in four generations.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE ICE CREAM FLAVOR REVEALED AS ONE CLASSIC TOPS EVERY STATE

"I can't mess with an 111-year-old lemon-ice recipe," O’Connor said. "We have generations of customers who are coming [to the shop]. They'll know."

DiCosmo's simple, high-quality ingredients, the company's authenticity and its family heritage are what's led the business to endure, O'Connor said.

"It's nostalgic. It tastes like something you might have had in your childhood."

"I squeeze every lemon by hand, and [the Italian ice] is made in small batches," she said. "The quality control is bar-none. We use real fruit, sugar and water, and that's what you taste. The fruit bursts in your mouth with flavor. It's not overly sweet."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The longer the mixture is kept cold, the bigger the ice crystals get, resulting in a different texture, O'Connor said.

Because the icy treat is made fresh throughout the day, it maintains its smooth consistency, she said. It's also the reason DiCosmo's is seeking franchisees — not space in the freezer aisles of retailers.

"There are no stabilizers or emulsifiers; that would make [the ice] freeze solid," she said.

"That's not what we're known for. We're known for our really clean, authentic fruit flavors and that texture where it melts in your mouth. To maintain standards, the same flavor and consistency, it has to be made fresh at each location."

O'Connor's parents transitioned the family store to an exclusive Italian ice shop, and new flavors, along with a machine to churn the ice mixture, were added along the way.

"If I stop doing this — and I love what I make — DiCosmo's stops," O'Connor said that she recalled one weekend while working at the shop prior to taking over the family business.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

DiCosmo's is "a true, fun, summertime experience," O'Connor said.

"It's nostalgic. It tastes like something you might have had in your childhood."

Creating a satisfying treat that people enjoy "motivates me," she added.

"It makes me feel proud," she said, crediting her "great team of employees" with the business' success.

Being a welcoming place for the community to gather is "so satisfying," she said.

"I didn't know it's what I wanted to do from the start, but I'm so glad I was born into this family where I can do this," O'Connor said.

World.title: Luigi Mangione's livestream stunt aims to get influencers to 'pressure' jurors: former prosecutor
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Luigi Mangione's push to livestream his murder trial isn't about transparency, it's a stunt designed to pressure jurors, a former federal prosecutor is arguing.

Lawyers for the accused UnitedHealthcare CEO assassin argued in a Friday filing that the media access rules for his state trial are unconstitutional, and said the proceedings should be livestreamed.

Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Mangione's attorney, said that her team wasn't consulted on media access for the upcoming September trial, and only became aware of a document titled "Media Access: PSNY v. Mangione" from an independent journalist on X.

MANGIONE LAWYERS SAY MEDIA LIMITS AT MURDER TRIAL ARE UNCONSTITUTIONAL, FEAR COURT WILL 'HAND-PICK' PRESS

Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani, president of West Coast Trial Lawyers, told Fox News Digital he believes Mangione's attorneys want all trial proceedings to be livestreamed to pressure jurors, noting it's unusual for defendants to want more publicity.

"The conventional wisdom is that the defense usually doesn't want high-profile cases broadcast. It can put implicit pressure on jurors to return a guilty verdict," Rahmani said. "Mangione is probably the most popular accused murderer that I've ever covered in the past 25 years. Has a fan base. There's upwards of 10 to 20 percent of the people who have been surveyed who believe that even if he did it, it was justified. And I think the defense knows this, and they know that more attention creates the possibility of jury nullification, or maybe even an acquittal."

PALISADES FIRE DEADLOCK FUELS FEAR THAT IDEOLOGY IS CREEPING INTO JURY BOX — AND MANGIONE COULD BE NEXT

Rahmani said the defense is counting on influencers to do what a courtroom sketch never could: keep the case viral.

"Obviously, those handwritten sketches, they're not as interesting as clips that you can post on TikTok or Instagram reels. The defense knows this and they want to take advantage of that influencer content and those viral videos," Rahmani said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Rahmani's argument tracks with the behavior of Mangione's supporters, who have lined up outside federal and state courthouses for a chance to see the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. One woman, Ashley, part of a group calling itself "The Mangionistas," told the New York Post she camped outside the court in December, and said it wasn't her first time.

SEND US A TIP

"I froze my a-- off last time so I brought a heater, a tent, everything,’’ another individual said.

GOT A TIP?

Rahmani said the strategy by Mangione's attorneys is to hopefully get enough influencers talking about the case to the point where it impacts jurors.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Jurors are supposed to decide the case solely based on the facts and evidence in the case, and they certainly shouldn't be on social media or AI or Google getting information about the case. But jurors are ordinary people, and they can't help but be influenced by these outside voices," he said. "And the defense knows this, and they know that more media attention likely means pressure on the jurors or potentially people that may be stealth jurors that may want to get on the panel to actually free Luigi in this case."

MANHATTAN DA'S OFFICE SAYS LUIGI MANGIONE DEFENSE SPREAD FALSE CLAIMS ABOUT MURDER TRIAL MEDIA PLAN

While Rahmani said it's clear what the defense is trying to do, their entire argument for getting the trial livestreamed is a stunt because New York state law prohibits it.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"There's no world where the defense is gonna get its request unless New York law changes or the judge does something extraordinary," Rahmani said. "People will think that there's some sort of cover-up because they've seen other high-profile trials livestreamed and they think that people may think that Luigi Mangione is not getting a fair trial because there's a lack of transparency."

Fox News Digital reached out to Mangione's attorneys for comment.

World.title: Mamdani faces questions over ties to outlet accused of antisemitic tropes
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing questions about his relationship with Uncivilized Media, a Qatar-based controversial outlet that has been accused of spreading antisemitic conspiracy theories.

Mamdani sat with the Uncivilized Media in 2023, and Fox News Digital found that he was still following the account on Instagram as of July 24, 2026. However, he appeared to have unfollowed the account, and as of July 27, 2026, he was no longer listed as a follower on Instagram. However, clips from his interview with Uncivilized Media were shared as collaborative posts on Instagram, meaning they appeared on both Mamdani's account and the outlet's account.

The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) and other experts on online antisemitism say that Uncivilized Media has produced content accusing Jews and Israelis of seeking global domination, being inherently colonialist and controlling the media, among other conspiracy theories. The organization noted several examples of what it said was Uncivilized Media pushing antisemitic tropes, including a July 2026 video in which Uncivilized Media accused Israelis of attempting to "colonize the world."

MAMDANI’S ‘DERANGED’ ISRAEL TAKE RESURFACES AS HE TARGETS NETANYAHU

Oren Segal, the ADL's senior vice president of counter-extremism and intelligence, told Fox News Digital that Uncivilized Media routinely promotes "classic tropes about Jews" in its content. He said that while the outlet's interviews with Mamdani did not focus on these conspiracies, some Jewish New Yorkers have wondered how exactly the mayor's views diverge from those held by the outlet.

"When one appears on any platform, it kind of normalizes the rest of the content that is out there," Segal told Fox News Digital, adding that neither he nor the ADL were accusing Mamdani of promoting or endorsing all of Uncivilized Media's content.

"What we are saying is that the connections between him and this particular digital entity raise questions for many New Yorkers who are curious as to whether the rest of the programming on there is something he believes in," Segal added.

In his interview with Uncivilized Media, which was originally posted on Sept. 11, 2023, Mamdani said the issue of the Palestinians was "central to my identity," framing it as a struggle for freedom.

"We say we care about freedom and justice and self-determination and yet, for some reason, we draw a line when it comes to Palestinians," Mamdani said.

He also spoke about how his background played a role in his views on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

"When you grow up as someone especially in the Third World, you have a very different understanding of the Palestinian struggle. It is one that is framed in terms of empathy and solidarity," Mamdani, who moved to New York at age seven, told the outlet.

In another video, which was posted days after the first clip, Mamdani said that progressive views and Muslim beliefs were in "inherent solidarity." He also identified himself as a socialist and "not simply progressive."

MAMDANI DOUBLES DOWN ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISM WHILE INSISTING WALL STREET, BUSINESS LEADERS CAN WORK WITH HIM

"What we also have now is a fight over what it means to be Muslim and what those Muslim values are. And I think that there is an attempt to frame those values [in opposition] to certain core progressive tenets," he said. "This idea of a single story that Muslims stand in opposition to queer rights, it attempts to flatten out a community whose history goes beyond hundreds of years in more than hundreds of countries."

The resurfacing of Mamdani's appearance with the outlet sparked concerns among some Jewish New Yorkers who believe their community's relationship with City Hall has deteriorated. Segal suggested that Mamdani could put worried New Yorkers at ease by publicly denouncing Uncivilized Media's spreading of antisemitic conspiracy theories.

"If Mayor Mamdani claims that he is building a better New York when there's many Jewish residents who consistently feel unheard, I think it's fair to ask him to clarify whether this program, that he has appeared on, represents his views on Israelis more broadly in terms of their content," Segal said.

The renewed scrutiny of Mamdani came after his statement last month on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In a video announcing that he did not have the legal authority to arrest the Israeli leader, Mamdani accused Netanyahu of being "a war criminal" and "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people."

Neither Mamdani's office nor Uncivilized Media responded to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

World.title: Iran’s regime won’t negotiate in good faith. Trump must break its grip
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

At Camp David, President Donald Trump signaled that Washington is entering a more dangerous phase in its confrontation with Iran. The objective is seemingly no longer limited to dismantling Iran’s nuclear infrastructure; it is now to weaken the Islamic Republic’s ability to govern, sustain itself, and ultimately survive.

America’s strategy toward Iran is undergoing its most significant shift in decades. The objective is apparently no longer simply to destroy Tehran’s nuclear program, but to systematically degrade the regime’s capacity to govern and sustain itself. At Camp David, President Donald Trump said the United States is prepared to intensify military pressure, warning that Washington would "hit them very hard" until the regime reaches a point where it "can’t go on anymore."

Trump’s repeated cancellations of planned large-scale strikes have raised questions about U.S. credibility and strategic coherence. Meanwhile, Tehran — backed by Moscow and Beijing — is exploiting that uncertainty, while Trump appears to be placing his hopes on a faction within Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.

IRANIANS SPEAK OUT OVER POSSIBLE TRUMP-REGIME DEAL

Many Iranians would welcome the ruling establishment’s humiliation, defeat, and eventual surrender. Although disrupting the regime’s critical infrastructure would impose temporary hardships, many opponents of the Islamic Republic see such suffering as the pain of childbirth — a difficult but necessary transition that could ultimately bring about the regime’s collapse.

Meanwhile, Tehran’s propaganda machine has threatened broad retaliation, warning that attacks on critical infrastructure will provoke a severe response. These statements indirectly acknowledge the regime’s preparation for a wider confrontation with the United States and Israel. They also raise the possibility that Tehran could activate dormant terrorist cells and other asymmetric assets in the United States and across the West — an arena in which the Islamic Republic has decades of experience.

The Iranian people are entering an even deeper period of hardship as the regime steadily loses control over large parts of the country. It could spiral into chaos at any moment. If, after the regime's collapse, a figure such as Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi does not lead a transitional government, Iran could face a bloodbath. The remnants of the Islamic Republic are likely to regroup through mosques and underground terrorist networks, preserving their ideology and continuing their campaign by other means. This risk cannot be ignored.

The current White House has shown no serious commitment to regime change in Iran. Defeating Islamist terrorism requires political resolve, strategic clarity, and a clear understanding of the threat. More than two decades into the 21st century, Washington has failed to defeat a regime that continues to serve the strategic interests of Moscow and Beijing, while much of Europe remains detached from reality. Israel alone has recognized that its security — and the emergence of a new Middle East — depends on regime change in Iran.

TRUMP KEEPS NEGOTIATING WHILE IRAN PLAYS THE LONG GAME AMERICA KEEPS MISSING

President Trump’s objective appears to be forcing Tehran back to the negotiating table. In my view, the ideological rigidity and fanaticism of the Shiite clerical establishment make that outcome unlikely. The regime has repeatedly shown that it would rather see Iran devastated than abandon its revolutionary ideology. This is no longer a conventional military campaign but a form of system warfare in which the regime’s critical vulnerability is no longer the IRGC or its nuclear facilities, but the infrastructure that enables it to survive.

The regime’s critical vulnerability now lies in its electricity grid, oil refineries, fuel distribution networks, command-and-control systems, communications infrastructure, and the institutions that sustain government. Disrupting these systems would have consequences far beyond physical destruction. The IRGC would struggle to coordinate nationwide operations, provincial control would weaken, and pressure on an already bankrupt government would intensify. This is the strategic logic behind targeting the regime’s infrastructure.

For forty-eight years, the Shiite clerical establishment has turned Iran into a military garrison and an ammunition depot. In pursuit of its revolutionary ideology, it has devastated the economy, plundered the nation’s wealth, and sacrificed Iran’s development for ideological expansion. For decades, much of the world ignored Israel’s warnings about the Islamic Republic. Only now is the international community beginning to recognize the scale of the security threat posed by Tehran’s state-sponsored Islamist terrorism.

IRAN IS NOT A NORMAL NATION YOU CAN MAKE DEALS WITH; IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT

America’s years of negotiating with Iran’s ruling clerical regime have produced little beyond delay, allowing Tehran to buy time while advancing its strategic objectives. Diplomacy with a regime built on terrorism and ideological expansion has repeatedly failed to deliver lasting security. Rather than seeking compromise, Tehran has used negotiations to outlast successive U.S. administrations. The result is a Middle East that continues to pay the price for Washington’s hesitation, while Israel confronts a threat it has long understood.

The Tehran regime and its military and intelligence institutions — including the Supreme National Security Council — have repeatedly threatened operations against the United States and Israel. Within the regime’s ideological worldview, mass-casualty attacks such as September 11 and October 7 are treated as instruments of political intimidation and ideological warfare. Khomeini and Khamenei may be gone, but the ideology they institutionalized endures. To preserve the regime, its leaders have repeatedly shown a willingness to commit acts of violence and repression.

The current White House has shown little commitment to pursuing regime change in Iran. Yet as long as Tehran continues to serve as a strategic partner of Moscow and Beijing, the challenge extends far beyond Iran itself. Israel has long recognized that lasting regional security depends on ending the Islamic Republic’s rule.

The path forward is clear: dismantling the infrastructure that sustains the Islamic Republic is the only way the United States and its allies can force a strategic recalibration in Tehran — or hasten the regime’s collapse. Anything less will allow the mullahs to continue their campaign of terrorism, instability, and ideological expansion. The next phase of this conflict will determine whether the Middle East remains hostage to a dying dictatorship — or finally breaks free.

CENTCOM’s strategic objectives may also require reassessment. Rather than focusing primarily on military facilities, its strategy should target the pillars that sustain the regime: cutting off the IRGC’s financial networks and proxies, disrupting its command-and-control capabilities, exposing the leadership’s corruption and hidden assets, denying access to surveillance technologies, and expanding secure communications for the Iranian people.

At the same time, lower-ranking military and security personnel should be told that those who refuse to repress civilians will have a future in a post-Islamic Republic Iran. External pressure without a credible transition plan risks producing chaos rather than change. The objective should be to dismantle the machinery of repression while preserving the Iranian people's ability to determine their own future.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Limited U.S. support could help spark a new popular uprising, accelerating the regime’s collapse. As Iran’s leaders remain hidden in tunnels and the regime’s security apparatus grows increasingly fragmented, Washington should prioritize coordinated covert clandestine operations, stronger protection for opposition figures, and a long-term transition strategy over election-driven diplomacy. Closer strategic coordination between the CIA and Mossad may also be essential to better understand and confront the ideological and operational roots of the radical Islamist threat that has spread since 1979 — a challenge successive U.S. administrations have too often underestimated. The people of Iran and Israel are already paying the price for a prolonged war of attrition. Unless Washington recognizes that the regime’s ideology leaves little room for compromise, the consequences will extend far beyond Iran.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The next phase of this conflict will determine not only the future of Iran, but the future balance of power across the Middle East.

World.title: WATCH: Smithsonian director admits she sees history as ‘tool’ of ‘social justice’ after explosive hearing
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

After an explosive series of congressional hearings on alleged woke "ideological capture" at the Smithsonian, a resurfaced video of a presentation by National Museum of American History Director Anthea Hartig shows her calling "history as a practice" a "prime tool of social justice."

In a series of July hearings on Capitol Hill, Hartig defended the Smithsonian’s record of objectivity and nonpartisanship. However, in a resurfaced presentation to University of California, Los Angeles students in February 2025, Hartig described "a number of ways in which your National Museum of American History is taking an equity-based, justice forward, community driven and necessarily humble approach to public history and to service."

Later in her presentation, Hartig asserted that the "United States’ long and violent racial history continues to be present in our reckoning, if you will."

She said that "redress in the form of reparation, of course, goes beyond acknowledgement of wrongdoing; it should leverage responsibility, it should think about the act of correction, as we pursue restorative justice and, for us [on the call], restorative justice through history."

TRUMP V. SMITHSONIAN: A TIMELINE OF HOW THE WHITE HOUSE FIGHT OVER 'WOKE' HISTORY UNFOLDED

During her testimony on Capitol Hill last month, Hartig stated: "Our work is governed by the Smithsonian standards of scholarship, accuracy, independence and nonpartisanship." She said, "the museum does not take sides in America's political debates," but instead, "We preserve and document the evidence of American life in all of its breadth, so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions."

However, in her presentation to UCLA, she asserted that "history as a practice … is for me a prime tool of social justice."

Hartig began her talk with a land acknowledgement and a slide showing a picture of an American flag defaced with words that appeared to read "Defund the Police." Her caption said the photo was from a Black Lives Matter protest in Washington, D.C., in 2020. Another photo Hartig showed later in the presentation depicted a protester holding a sign that read, "America loving you is complicated."

She remarked that the museum opened in 1964 as "this kind of Cold War, you know, ‘We’re going to be the best and most technologically advanced country in the nation and we’re going to show everyone how we did that’ … We clearly have moved away from that."

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

Instead, Hartig highlighted what she called the museum’s "bold new vision" to become the "most accessible, inclusive, relevant, and sustainable public history institution in the country." This, the vision states, will allow the museum to "serve an audience that reflects the full racial, class, gender, ethnic, and geographic demographics of the United States."

To this end, Hartig said the museum "joined a very collaborative Smithsonian-wide collecting effort around Black Lives Matter … to document and preserve and share objects focused on Black Lives Matter to show the history of the movement starting in 2012."

She shared a picture of protest signs outside the White House from the summer of 2020 and spoke highly of "these phenomenal, ephemeral statements, signs … expressing that kind of very heartfelt and incredibly poignant [message]."

Hartig also praised an anti-ICE organization called "Tsuru for Solidarity" as a "truly remarkable group," highlighting its collaboration with the Black Lives Matter movement.

According to its website, Tsuru for Solidarity is a "nonviolent, direct action project of Japanese American social justice advocates and allies working to end detention sites and support directly impacted immigrant and refugee communities that are being targeted by racist, inhumane immigration policies." Its website also states, "We stand on the moral authority of Japanese Americans who suffered the atrocities and legacy of U.S. concentration camps during WWII and we say, ‘Stop Repeating History!’"

FORMER DEMOCRATIC STAFFERS, DEI LEADERS SHAPE SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP AMID POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Besides the Black Lives Matter initiative, Hartig said the museum is pursuing a "proactive multilingual strategy to support language justice."

She explained that "the idea, of course, [is] that everyone has the right to communicate in the language in which they feel most comfortable to be understood and to understand."

To this end, she said that since the fall of 2019, "all exhibitions and signage and digital projects will be at least bilingual in English and Spanish and a number of them in more languages depending on the project and communities of origin."

Hartig asserted, "We’re under attack for speaking complicated truths" and urged students to "raise your voices and speak them together."

She said, "It continues to grow resolute in my mind, [history] is the key that unlocks the mysteries of humanity, of meaning, of place, of conquest, of love, power, authority and self."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"We are tellers of stories and seekers of truths, hopefully embracers of nuance, ambassadors of empathy and defenders of inalienable rights," she said.
