World.title: Croatian Pizza Prices Spark Debate as Bill Goes Viral
World.content:
August the 4th, 2026 – Croatian pizza prices have sparked fresh debate as a bill of 32 euros issued in Stari Grad on Hvar goes viral across social media.

Debates over prices on the Croatian coast have once again erupted on social media, with a restaurant bill from the island of Hvar becoming the latest trigger for a wider discussion about the cost of summer holidays in Croatia. Poslovni reports that this latest price-related controversy began after a guest shared a receipt from a pizzeria in Stari Grad, where a large pizza cost 22 euros. The post quickly spread online, dividing opinions between two opposing camps.

Some users described such prices as completely unreasonable and a sign of growing greed in the tourism sector. Others argued that restaurants clearly display their menus and prices, meaning guests can see the costs in advance and decide whether they want to order. The fact that another seaside bill became a viral topic highlights how strongly food and service prices continue to shape conversations during every tourist season. The debate has grown beyond the price of one pizza, becoming part of a larger discussion about Croatia’s tourism model.

22 euros is steep compared to a 7.50 euro pizza in italy

Soon, visitors began sharing their own experiences and comparing Croatian coastal prices with those in other popular European destinations. One social media user compared the situation with southern Italy, saying that in a restaurant in Ercolano, near Naples, a pizza cost just 7.50 euros, a beer 3 euros, and a bottle of white wine 10 euros.

Others shared less positive experiences from Croatian islands. One visitor said that while the island of Vis was beautiful, the prices were too high. She described paying €120 per person for a seven-hour speedboat excursion that included visits to three caves and two beaches, but without lunch included. She also pointed out that entering one of the caves cost an additional €15, even for those who chose to swim there themselves.

However, not everyone believes the criticism is justified. Some commenters argued that visitors simply choose where they travel and where they eat according to their own budgets. “Everyone goes where the food and prices suit them,” one comment said, summarising the opinion of those who believe customers have the final choice.

Many also pointed out that high prices will continue as long as there is demand and people willing to pay them.

“While there are people who will gladly pay 22 euros for a pizza, there will be prices like this. But tourism cannot rely on this forever,” one user wrote, warning that the current model may not be sustainable in the long term. Others noted that expensive pizzas are not only found on the coast, mentioning examples from Zagreb as well, expanding the discussion beyond seasonal tourism.

An even more expensive pizza becomes the symbol of the debate

The most attention, however, was attracted by a comment from a man who claimed that he had seen an even more expensive pizza on the island of Brač. “There are also pizzas for 32 euros. If it doesn’t suit you, the door is open for you to leave and go elsewhere,” he wrote.

The comment quickly became a symbol of the argument that prices are ultimately determined by supply and demand, with businesses charging what customers are prepared to pay. Another theory that appeared in the discussion was that some tourists deliberately visit the most expensive restaurants so they can later complain online and share their bills on social media, gaining attention. “They go there on purpose so they can complain about high prices afterwards,” one commenter suggested.

Guests complain, but the spending continues…

Although complaints about Croatian prices return every summer, financial data paints a more complex picture. Examples of expensive bills continue to circulate online, including a case of visitors from neighbouring Bosnia and Herzegovina who reportedly paid more than 50 euros for a jumbo pizza and two coffees near Dubrovnik, as well as a British tourist who paid a whole 42 euros for just two drinks in Split.

However, spending figures show that tourists are still opening their wallets. According to data from Croatia’s Tax Administration, consumer spending during the summer months has continued to grow. In July, the total value of fiscalised receipts increased by almost 24 percent compared with the same month last year, reaching 6.8 billion euros.

The hospitality sector also recorded growth, with more than seven percent more receipts issued and their total value increasing by over 11 percent. Tourism analysts say this shows that visitors continue to spend despite complaints, although they warn that such a trend may not be sustainable forever.

The picture is not the same everywhere

A closer look at the tourism sector shows that success is not evenly distributed. While luxury hotels and high-end campsites are recording strong occupancy and increased revenue, many small private accommodation providers and some restaurants are facing difficulties. June 2026’s figures showed a decline of seven percent in arrivals and six percent in overnight stays compared with the previous year, with the largest drops recorded in Istria, Kvarner and Zadar County.

The data suggests a growing divide within Croatian tourism. Luxury segments continue to perform well, while businesses offering average services at increasingly high prices are finding it harder to attract guests. Tourists appear to be paying closer attention to value for money and are becoming less willing to spend large amounts on experiences that do not match the expected quality.

Market rules apply, but guests are becoming more demanding

Tourism experts have repeatedly warned about price increases that are not matched by improvements in quality. While the government and the Ministry of Tourism have called for more reasonable pricing policies, Boris Žgomba, president of the Croatian Chamber of Commerce’s Association of Travel Agencies, has stressed that prices are ultimately determined by the market and the relationship between supply and demand. Croatia has positioned itself alongside other Mediterranean destinations such as Italy and Spain in terms of pricing, while Dubrovnik regularly ranks among the most expensive cities in the region.

At the same time, travellers are increasingly searching for authentic experiences, local culture and quieter destinations. This could create opportunities for parts of Croatia’s tourism industry that adapt to changing expectations.

If prices continue rising without a corresponding improvement in quality, some tourists may turn towards more affordable destinations such as Albania, which has experienced strong tourism growth by attracting visitors who find Croatia or Greece too expensive. As another busy summer season unfolds, prices on the Croatian coast and islands remain one of the most debated topics in Croatia, raising a continuing question: where is the line between market logic and genuine hospitality?

World.title: Golf center and private residences planned near Tartu
World.content:
A comprehensive plan for the Ilmatsalu area envisions a golf village, two artificial lakes and a neighborhood of single-family homes on the site of former fish farming ponds.

Ilmatsalu is a small borough about 11 kilometers west of downtown Tartu. The 200-hectare planning area covers land on both sides of the Ilmatsalu River, including the site of the former fish farming ponds.

According to Indrek Ranniku, head of comprehensive planning at Tartu's Spatial Planning Department, the project's environmental impacts have also been thoroughly assessed.

"The most important issue is water flow — how to ensure the artificial lakes function properly, how to maintain the existing Ilmatsalu reservoir and how to preserve the ecosystem of the Ilmatsalu River. Through the environmental impact assessment process, we've been able to define these issues quite precisely because this is the most sensitive topic for both residents and nature. As far as nature is concerned, it's also important to note that this is a former fish farming area that has become overgrown over the years," Ranniku said.

The golf center will be developed by Tartu Golf LLC, a company registered four months ago.

"The area is surrounded by State Forest Management Center (RMK) forests, which are designated as part of the green network under both the county plan and the city's comprehensive plan. It includes a core area identified in the county plan. All of that will remain intact and there are no issues with it. The golf course will occupy only a small part of the area, on two properties, and the conditions have been set so that the green network will continue to function," Ranniku said, adding that the plan has been approved by nature conservation authorities.

Under the plans, the major housing development could double the borough's population. Ranniku said this would also require reconstruction of the main street and would finally bring a grocery store to Ilmatsalu. If needed, the school could also be expanded and a new kindergarten built.

"The comprehensive plan also reserves land for a kindergarten if the need arises, so a site has been set aside on the banks of the Ilmatsalu River," Ranniku said.

Eve Kivilo, an active member of the Ilmatsalu community, said the comprehensive plan is currently one of the community's main topics of conversation.

"Younger people may welcome it much more positively than the older generation who are perhaps a little more apprehensive about change. But we hope the city and best planning practices will find the right balance, so that what's already here isn't neglected and people don't focus too much on all the new potential opportunities and everything that may come. We hope they won't forget what already exists in the area," Kivilo said.

The Ilmatsalu comprehensive plan will be presented at a public meeting in the school auditorium on the evening of August 10. It will remain on public display through August 17.

World.title: Former defense chief Riho Ühtegi bows out of Estonian presidency race
World.content:
One of the figures who stated they were interested in running at next month's presidential election has announced their withdrawal from the race, Postimees reported .

Maj. Gen. (Ret.) Riho Ühtegi, a former Defense League commander, was put forward as a potential candidate in early July, but has stepped down, citing health issues.

"I am withdrawing from the race for the presidency of the Republic of Estonia as this week I received confirmation of a serious health condition," Ühtegi told Postimees.

"When I had agreed to run, I set myself two factors that would have ruled out my candidacy, and one of these was my health. Unfortunately, I never imagined I would actually have to make such a decision," he added.

Ühtegi, 62, who described his worldview as broadly conservative, was proposed by five public figures: Composer Sven Grünberg, businessman Hugo Osula, entrepreneur and filmmaker Kris Taska, actor and director Hendrik Toompere, and political analyst Raivo Vare, who listed his level-headedness and strong security- and crisis-management experience as plus points.

Ühtegi had met with opposition party Isamaa in connection with a potential bid for the presidency.

Ühtegi: I don't see any strong presidential candidates emerging so far

As for who might be the next head of state, Ühtegi said he "didn't see any strong candidates" from the current field, calling them out of touch. "I have been among the people, and I know how important that truly is for the average person. Sitting in an office in Tallinn or Brussels, you can never gain that understanding," he went on.

Ühtegi said ordinary people have become disillusioned with the state. "Estonia's main problems are a divided society, security challenges, and our future," he added, pointing to a lack of certainty.

"Will we still exist as a nation and a state? Those are the questions we need to be thinking about today," he added.

To run, a candidate must give their consent, while a majority of at least 68 votes in the 101-seat Riigikogu is needed to get elected. If three rounds of voting draw a blank, the process moves to the 208-member regional electoral college.

The formal presidential candidate nomination process runs August 21-24, while the Riigikogu ballots are scheduled for September 2-3.

Current head of state Alar Karis is not seeking a second term.

Editor's note: This article was updated to include further comment from Ühtegi.

World.title: Gambling restriction list nears 21,000 as Estonia plans law review
World.content:
The number of people with gambling addictions has grown in recent years, with nearly 21,000 people now on the self-imposed gambling restriction list. The Ministry of Finance plans to review the Gambling Act next year and update the details of how the restriction list is compiled.

Under the current plan, the changes could take effect in the middle of the year after next. The state collected €61 million in gambling taxes last year.

The number of people on the list has steadily increased over the past three years. In 2023, the list included 17,203 people.

One person may have restrictions on several types of games. Restrictions on games of chance now apply to 20,628 people, sports betting restrictions to 9,767 people, and lottery restrictions to 5,968 people. Sports betting restrictions have increased by 348 since the beginning of the year.

A person is added to the list indefinitely based on their own written application, and they must specify a period after which they may submit a new application to be removed from the list.

The period cannot be shorter than six months or longer than three years, said Jekaterina Nikitina, head of the excise department at the Tax and Customs Board.

"In our view, the fact that the number of people who have set restrictions for themselves has increased over the years shows that people are increasingly aware of the player protection mechanisms we have. These mechanisms work very well; otherwise, players would not use them," Nikitina said.

Under the Gambling Act, gambling operators must implement measures to ensure that people on the list cannot play the types of games they have restricted.

Rainer Osanik Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi /ERR

Rainer Osanik, head of the financial information policy department at the Ministry of Finance, said only isolated cases have occurred where companies failed to meet this requirement.

"Gambling operators comply with this requirement quite diligently. If a person is on the list and they are still allowed to play, the operator must refund the money the person lost. But the opposite also applies: if the person wins, they must return the winnings," Osanik said.

Next year, the Ministry of Finance plans to review the Gambling Act, including the rules for compiling the restriction list. Osanik said one problem is that a gambling addict often does not want to add themselves to the list.

"No one else can currently add them to the list, but family members of a gambling addict often suffer. The system should allow a person to be added to the list on certain additional grounds, either at the initiative of a family member or by court order. Estonian law does not currently allow this. We will now begin analyzing how this could be done," Osanik said.

World.title: Estonia secures up to €2.34 billion EU loan for defense investments
World.content:
Estonia will receive up to €2.34 billion in long-term loans for defense investments under a funding agreement signed with the European Commission through the SAFE (Security Action for Europe) program. The loan will help speed up capability upgrades planned by the Ministry of Defense.

Europe's security situation requires member states to rapidly strengthen their defenses while the continent's defense industry expands production capacity. Estonia has decided to allocate more than five percent of GDP annually to national defense in the coming years, allowing planned investments to move forward faster and at a larger scale.

"Using the SAFE loan is a sensible way to finance the strengthening of defense capability. As a major issuer, the European Union can borrow on more favorable terms than Estonia, which helps save on interest costs," said Janno Luurmees, head of the state treasury department at the Ministry of Finance.

He said the loan's 45‑year term allows repayments to be spread over a longer period. "When taking on debt obligations, it's useful to combine different instruments, sources and maturities to secure the best possible terms. This way we can make the necessary defense investments and reduce pressure on state budgets in the coming years," he said.

Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur said that 2.34 billion euros is exactly the amount Estonia wanted, meaning the loan was received in full as requested.

"Our interest in using the SAFE loan was connected to what we can finance through SAFE, and it can be used to fund defense‑capability developments that are of European origin. This concerns ammunition, certain weapons systems, and likewise air defense," Pevkur said.

SAFE is part of the European Union's ReArm Europe package, aimed at accelerating defense capability development. Through the mechanism, the EU will raise up to €150 billion from capital markets and provide the funds to member states as long-term loans for defense investments.

Kadri Peeters. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Kadri Peeters, deputy secretary general for defense capability at the Ministry of Defense, said Europe's rapidly changing security environment demands more defense and faster action from the entire alliance.

"Estonia's historic decision to allocate more than five percent of GDP annually to defense, combined with the EU's SAFE loan mechanism, allows us to carry out critical investments outlined in NATO defense plans and our development programs at a significantly faster pace and larger scale," Peeters said, adding that major procurements in the coming years will directly affect security in Estonia and the region.

One condition of the SAFE mechanism is joint procurement. To support the development of Europe's defense industry, at least 65 percent of the final components of purchased products must come from the European Union.

The Ministry of Defense will use the SAFE loan to strengthen air defense, acquire military vehicles, artillery shells and other ammunition, and support Ukraine with unmanned aerial vehicles.

Estonia submitted its final SAFE loan application — the defense industry investment plan — to the European Commission in November 2025. Procurements and deliveries under the plan must be completed by 2030.

Estonia previously borrowed €230 million from the European Commission's TERA funding to retroactively cover the government's extraordinary expenses in 2020 to mitigate the impact of the Covid‑19 epidemic.

This article was updated to include comments by Hanno Pevkur.

Reservists practiced live fire with Estonia's HIMARS off the coast of Saaremaa for the first time on July 11, 2025. Source: EDF/ kpr/OR-2 Maria Tammeaid

World.title: Influencer's sex crimes database website taken offline over privacy concerns
World.content:
A website set up by a noted influencer has been taken offline over privacy and safety concerns, following an order from the state Data Protection Inspectorate (AKI).

The site ettevaatust.ee (English: "Watch out") was set up by blogger and content creator Mallukas, real name Mallu Mariann Treimann-Legrant, and her husband, Tomas Märten Legrant.

It aimed to compile profiles of people with criminal convictions, mainly relating to sexual offenses, abuse, and domestic violence. The information was drawn from publicly available sources. Users could view the individuals' offense details, together with direct links to their entries in the criminal records database.

In June, the AKI ordered the site's activities to stop, saying the website effectively functioned as an alternative database of criminal records. The AKI demanded the removal of offenders' names, photographs, and references to court rulings. As of Tuesday, the site was down, blocked by web hosting provider Zone.

Tomas Märten Legrant shared correspondence via social media with Zone's customer support team informing him that public access to ettevaatust.ee had now been restricted on the basis of an enforcement order issued by the AKI. The website owners can still access the site and its backend.

"You will retain access to the website files through the file manager. In addition, we will send you separate login credentials that will allow you to view the website's homepage," the message said. The same message stated restoring public access would require confirmation or consent from the AKI.

Typing in the site's url as of Wednesday morning revealed this message. Source: Screenshot

The website's operator had been ordered to comply with the inspectorate's decision by June 29, but Mallu Mariann Treimann-Legrant, as co-founder of the site, disagreed with the authority's decision, questioning why it needed to be regulated and why criminals needed to be "protected."

"I'm not talking about some random pickpocket – I'm talking about criminals who permanently destroy the lives of small children and women. Why do these need protection?" Treimann-Legrant inquired at the time.

AKI Director General Pille Lehis said, when the decision was issued, that a criminal records database, or anything closely resembling one, can only be maintained by the state or under state supervision.

The site was created through an NGO and made use of user submissions. The creators said the site would improve public safety and had been inspired by reports of a convicted sex offender still employed at a horse riding school.

Within 24 hours of going live in March this year, ettevaatust.ee received 370 submissions. Treimann-Legrant and her partner said they verified entries and have corrected errors involving the mis-identification of people, for instance, by incorrect photos being published. Another issue was that of individuals with no connection to the crimes in question but who shared the same name as those convicted.

The AKI opened supervisory proceedings shortly after the site went live, stating republished public data must still comply with privacy, transparency, accuracy, and victim protection rules.

Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200) argued Estonia's regulated criminal records system already balances transparency and privacy, warning unofficial "exposure lists" risk errors, vigilantism, and harm to innocent people.

World.title: U.S. weapons paused by Iran conflict set to reach Estonia within weeks
World.content:
U.S. arms deliveries that were temporarily halted will reach Estonia already in the coming weeks, Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur says. The exception is ATACMS missiles for HIMARS, which cannot currently be obtained from the Americans because of the war in Iran.

Pevkur said in mid-July that an agreement had been reached with the Americans to resume deliveries and that all ordered munitions — except ATACMS — had been cleared for transport. At the time, he estimated that different types of ammunition should arrive in Estonia within the coming months, with delivery timelines depending on logistics.

By early August, the situation had changed enough that delivery times are no longer measured in months but in weeks, Pevkur said on Wednesday.

Hanno Pevkur. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

"In essence, the situation is the same — deliveries are underway, and as far as I know, the question is no longer months but weeks. We do not want to disclose the exact delivery date for security reasons," he said.

However, Estonia still cannot obtain ATACMS tactical missiles — with a range of up to 300 kilometers — used by the HIMARS multiple rocket launcher.

"There is no change regarding ATACMS. As we see, there is still no solution in Iran, and therefore we have no additional information about ATACMS. We are moving forward with all other deliveries, but ATACMS remains on hold," Pevkur said.

The Estonian Defense Forces currently have six HIMARS (M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System) launchers. In April, the Defense Investment Center and U.S. defense contractor Lockheed Martin signed a contract for three additional HIMARS launchers, expected to arrive in Estonia in 2027.

World.title: Prison service says Tartu recruitment drive is ahead of schedule
World.content:
Recruitment is on schedule and the first officers have already been hired, the prison service has said, as it prepares for the arrival of several hundred prisoners from Sweden.

Under an agreement struck between Estonia and Sweden, several hundred prisoners will be sent to serve part of their sentences in the prison in south Estonia to alleviate overcrowding in Swedish jails.

Tartu Prison is now seeking nearly 300 new employees. Although the first recruitment round took place in June, the prison opened its doors on Tuesday to nearly 100 interested visitors for a career day.

The prison's director said interest is high and recruitment is ahead of schedule. "We have already had nearly 400 active applicants and have already hired 20 of them. I would say that nearly 70 people are currently in the active recruitment process to come and work at Tartu Prison," said Merle Ulst, director of Tartu Prison.

The applicants have varied backgrounds. They include both young people looking for their first work experience and former prison employees who had been laid off and have now found their way back to the profession.

"During the day, they were able to get acquainted with our different areas of work, including trying out a cell search themselves, watching a dog demonstration training session and seeing the prison transport buses," said Konstantin Nikiforov, chief specialist at Tartu Prison.

The first Swedish inmates are expected to arrive in Tartu as early as this month. According to the prison director, everything is ready for their arrival. "The inmates will arrive in small groups, and I can say that by the end of September we will have 100 inmates here," Ulst said.

The prison service said applicants must be over 18 years old and need to pass a background check and physical fitness tests.

A good grasp of Estonian is needed, but there is no need to worry about English skills: being able to manage polite communication is sufficient.

"The most important thing is that the person has the will to work in this kind of institution, with these kinds of people, and to do this work with dedication and motivation," Nikiforov said.

According to the prison's management, the current recruitment drive will not be the last, and additional employees will be trained as needed.

World.title: Tartu students prefer rental apartments to dorms
World.content:
Students moving to Tartu to begin their studies are increasingly choosing rental apartments over university dormitories.

About 25 percent of the University of Tartu's students live in Tartu Student Village housing, but university dormitories are no longer the first choice for many students who are increasingly turning to the private rental market, said Karen Tuul, accommodation manager at Tartu Student Village.

The decline in the number of international students at the University of Tartu may also be a key reason demand for dormitory housing has fallen, Tuul said.

"At the moment, we even have some double rooms sitting vacant," she added.

Tuul said that by now, most University of Tartu students who wanted a dormitory room have secured one. Single rooms and apartment-style one- and two-room units remain the most popular options and have the longest waiting lists. University of Tartu students receive priority for housing at Tartu Student Village, though students from other higher education institutions are also on the waiting list.

Ene Linnok, chief administrative specialist at Tartu Health Care College, said the number of dormitory applications submitted this year is about 25 percent lower than last year. Even so, there is still a waiting list for available rooms.

"The college continuously monitors dormitory occupancy and rooms that become available are offered to applicants on the waiting list when necessary. Dormitory places are allocated according to the established procedure and a single waiting list, ensuring equal treatment for all applicants," Linnok said.

According to Roland Aik Kask, manager of the Rohemu Campus dormitory at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, more housing applications have been submitted this year than last year. The dormitory has about 900 places, around 70 percent of which are occupied by Estonian University of Life Sciences students.

"We've made many improvements in recent years. We renovated the facilities and made them more functional and we also updated the contract terms so that cooperation between residents and management runs even more smoothly," Kask said.

Tartu Student Village operates eight apartment units across the city. Rates vary, with the least expensive rooms costing about €85 a month and studio apartments costing up to €475. Monthly rent at the Tartu Health Care College dormitory depends on the room type and occupancy arrangement and ranges from €53 to €165. At Rohemu Campus, monthly accommodation fees range from €165 to €600, depending on the type of accommodation and the contract.

Tartu Student Village has a total of 2,681 places across its eight dormitories. Rohemu Campus has about 900 places, while Tartu Health Care College offers nearly 300 accommodation places.

World.title: Iraq in talks with Iran to facilitate vessel transit through Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that discussions are taking place with Iran regarding the transit of oil tankers via the Strait of Hormuz, with an anticipated agreement in the near future.

In a statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair stated that the economic and political discussions held during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran addressed approaches to expand cooperation and resulted in signing several agreements.

The Iraqi delegation held talks with Iranian counterparts to ensure the safe transit of vessels across the Strait of Hormuz and protect oil shipments, according to Khudair.

The oil minister stressed that the policy of the Iraqi government is based on building communication channels and partnerships with neighboring countries to support the national economy.

The two parties’ discussions aim to avert future interruptions to Iraqi oil exports amid growing regional maritime concerns.

As Baghdad depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz, it seeks to secure a deal for the safe passage of oil shipments through the waterway.

While Iran has previously shown a willingness to make exceptions for friendly or non-hostile neighbors, practical implementation and approval processes remain a primary focus of continuing discussions.

World.title: Iraq’s liquidity crisis causes delays in paying public servants
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is experiencing a serious financial and liquidity problem, causing delays in paying state employees.

The fall in income from oil, due to the difficulties of exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, has put the Finance Ministry of Iraq in a deficit by trillions of dinars.

The Iraqi government is considering home loans to finance its enormous monthly salaries.

Crude oil exports, which account for approximately 90 percent of Iraq’s federal income, fell dramatically because of the military operations in the region and maritime shipping difficulties.

Iraq requires between 8 and 11 trillion Iraqi dinars ($6.1 billion to $8.4 billion) every month to pay millions of governmental staff and pensioners.

The country’s income fell significantly below expenditure demands, resulting in a large monthly shortfall and an acute cash crisis.

Payrolls have experienced extraordinary delays, causing public concern and reducing local economic activity.

Financing shortfalls have put a burden on government-owned enterprises, particularly drug delivery in the health sector.

Authorities aim to engage in temporary local borrowing to avoid incurring further international debt, as well as long-term calls for diversified state resources.

World.title: Dana Gas, Crescent Petroleum supply Baghdad with gas for electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum said on Tuesday that they started supplying the electricity ministry with natural gas from the Khor Mor field in Iraqi Kurdistan under an agreement to support the country’s electricity output.

An agreement was reached last December between the Electricity Ministry and the two companies to supply 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Khor Mor facility to the Taza gas-fired power plant in Kirkuk province for a period of one year.

The step took place after a project to increase the production capacity of the Khor Mor gas field to 750 million cubic feet per day was completed.

The completion of the expansion project increased the availability of additional gas quantities to local markets through the pipeline network, as reported by Shafaq News.

Majid Jafar, CEO of Crescent Petroleum and Managing Director of Dana Gas, stated that the gas transfer to the Electricity Ministry in Baghdad marks an important milestone in Iraqi Kurdistan’s gas sector growth.

Jafar explained that this development will address the growing demand for electricity and enhance the services offered to residents.

Richard Hall, CEO of Dana Gas Group, described the deal as an important step reflecting the outcomes of the production growth program.

According to Hall, the agreement paves the way for enhanced collaboration within Iraq’s energy sector, strengthens energy security, and contributes to the stability of the electricity grid.

The Khor Mor gas project provides the fuel required to produce more than 80 percent of the energy in Iraqi Kurdistan, which supplies power to over eight million people.

World.title: Iraq unveils tourism vision 2035 to attract 10 million visitors
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has unveiled an ambitious long-term strategy to transform its tourism sector, aiming to attract 10 million visitors by 2035 through infrastructure upgrades, workforce development, and the preservation of the country’s rich historical, cultural, and religious heritage.

The Iraqi Tourism Authority announced on Tuesday that it has finalized the Iraq Tourism Vision 2035, a roadmap launched under the slogan “A Prosperous and Competitive Iraq.” The initiative is designed to position Iraq as a leading tourism destination in the region while supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

Ali Yassin, spokesperson for the Tourism Authority, said the agency will begin organizing workshops in Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, Karbala, and Erbil to present the vision’s objectives and implementation mechanisms to stakeholders across the country.

The workshops aim to engage local governments, tourism professionals, and investors in executing the strategy over the coming decade.

According to the authority, the plan seeks to attract 10 million tourists by 2035, with a focus on promoting Iraq’s archaeological, cultural, religious, and natural attractions.

Officials said achieving the target will require significant investment in tourism infrastructure, including improving transportation, accommodation, visitor services, and restoring key heritage sites across the country.

The strategy also calls for the rehabilitation and maintenance of archaeological landmarks, museums, religious sites, and other destinations that showcase Iraq’s diverse historical legacy.

The Tourism Vision 2035 is built around three strategic pillars: integration, sustainability, and quality.

Officials said these principles will guide efforts to create a more competitive tourism industry while ensuring long-term preservation of Iraq’s cultural and natural resources.

The plan also emphasizes improving coordination among government institutions and the private sector to encourage investment and strengthen the country’s tourism ecosystem.

In addition to infrastructure projects, the Tourism Authority highlighted the importance of developing skilled professionals capable of supporting the industry’s growth.

The vision includes programs to strengthen the capabilities of workers in the tourism sector through training and capacity-building initiatives, recognizing that qualified personnel are essential to delivering high-quality visitor experiences.

The Tourism Authority said the long-term strategy reflects its commitment to restoring Iraq’s position as a prominent international tourism destination.

By combining investment in infrastructure, heritage preservation, sustainability, and workforce development, officials hope the plan will contribute to economic growth while showcasing Iraq’s unique cultural and historical assets to visitors from around the world.

World.title: Iraq liquidity crisis does not mean bankruptcy, says government financial adviser
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq liquidity crisis should not be interpreted as a sign that the country is running out of money or facing bankruptcy, according to government financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Salih. He emphasized that the Iraqi government retains sufficient financial and administrative tools to continue paying salaries and meeting its core obligations despite ongoing cash flow pressures.

Speaking to Shafaq News on Tuesday, Salih explained that the current challenge stems from timing mismatches between oil revenues entering the treasury and the government’s monthly expenditure commitments, particularly public sector salaries.

Salih stressed that Iraq’s financial pressures are primarily linked to liquidity management rather than a shortage of national wealth.

According to him, the government’s current challenges include:

Timing differences between oil revenue receipts and monthly spending obligations.

High levels of public expenditure.

Continued expansion of public sector employment.

Weak non-oil revenues.

Regional tensions affecting trade and oil exports.

He said these factors have created temporary liquidity pressures but do not indicate a severe financial crisis.

The financial adviser said the government can continue paying salaries and maintaining essential public services through several financial management tools.

These include:

Efficient liquidity management.

Prioritizing essential expenditures such as salaries.

Rescheduling non-urgent investment projects when necessary.

Improving tax and fee collection.

Reducing financial waste.

Increasing non-oil government revenues.

Salih also noted that domestic or external borrowing remains available if required, provided borrowing remains within safe public debt limits and supports financial stability.

Looking ahead, Salih said Iraq must accelerate long-term economic reforms to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

He highlighted several priorities:

Diversifying oil export routes.

Developing transportation and energy infrastructure.

Expanding non-oil revenue sources.

Building a more resilient economy capable of absorbing regional and global shocks.

He concluded that sustainable financial stability cannot rely solely on oil income and will require broader economic diversification and structural reforms.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports surpass 1.25 million bpd in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July 2026 by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June, according to Attaqa News.

Despite this partial recovery, Iraqi shipments remain significantly lower than pre-war levels, reflecting a 63 percent decline from the July 2025 figure of 3.38 million barrels per day.

With the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad’s major marine trade route, strains on the state budget are increasing due to declining oil earnings.

The decrease in revenue from oil exports has driven the Iraqi government to accelerate its search for alternative land routes to export crude oil via neighboring countries.

In July, Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports reached one million barrels per day for the first time since March 2026, marking the end of a steep fall.

The country’s oil exports totaled 3.31 million barrels per day in January, 3.34 million barrels per day in February, 542,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, 98,000 barrels per day in May, 493,000 barrels per day in June, and 1.25 million barrels per day in July.

The figures show that Iraq’s average offshore oil exports fell by 60 percent between January and July 2026, hitting 1.31 million barrels per day compared to 3.33 million barrels per day during the same period in 2025.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Iraq clarifies role in oil tanker transit through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has clarified that it is not responsible for the movement of crude oil tankers after they leave Iraqi export terminals, emphasizing that buyers assume full responsibility for transporting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The statement comes as Iraq continues to navigate regional security challenges affecting energy exports, while officials report gradual improvements in crude oil sales in recent months.

Oil Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said Iraq continues to sell crude oil under the Free on Board (FOB) system, meaning ownership and responsibility for the cargo transfer to the buyer once the shipment is loaded at Iraqi ports.

According to Al-Rikabi, tankers carrying Iraqi crude continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz after departing export terminals. However, he stressed that the ministry is not responsible for the vessels’ navigation routes or for securing the necessary transit approvals.

“The ministry sells crude oil at the port, after which the buyer assumes responsibility for transporting and managing the shipment,” Al-Rikabi said.

He added that the ministry neither owns the tankers nor oversees their operations once they leave Iraqi waters.

Despite transferring responsibility to buyers, Al-Rikabi said the Oil Ministry continues monitoring tanker movements through international vessel-tracking systems.

He noted that Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) follows shipments until they reach their destination refineries, allowing authorities to track export deliveries without directly managing vessel operations.

Some tankers transporting Iraqi crude carry cargoes of up to 2 million barrels, according to the ministry.

Al-Rikabi also indicated that Iraq’s oil export performance has improved steadily in recent months despite disruptions linked to the regional security situation and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said sales last month exceeded those recorded in the previous month, continuing a gradual recovery following earlier export challenges caused by tensions affecting maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes, carrying a significant share of global crude exports, making uninterrupted transit critical for Iraq’s energy sector and international oil markets.

World.title: Iraq launches 3,000-cubic-meter gas storage facility in Najaf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated a gas storage project as part of the Oil Ministry’s efforts to raise storage capacity in line with current operations to boost gas output.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry revealed Monday the start of trial operations at a new gas storage facility in the central Iraqi province of Najaf.

Undersecretary for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber said in a statement that the new gas depot has a storage capacity of 3,000 cubic meters and is part of efforts to boost production and storage capabilities, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The step also reflects the ministry’s efforts to develop the transportation, storage, and distribution systems of liquefied gas, according to Saber.

The Iraqi official explained that the inauguration of the depot at the trial operation stage is certainly an important milestone in improving the capacity of strategic reserves and increasing the flexibility of the supply system.

The initiative will ensure that the requirements for liquefied gas in the central provinces and other cities are adequately met.

The delivery of liquefied gas to the new depot via pipelines, as opposed to tanker trucks, will adhere to safety standards and enhance the stability of supplies.

Who is Saurav Das

NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol has increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming that motorists are paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country have been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised.He further alleged that consumers are paying more due to the lower mileage of ethanol-blended fuel.âOn the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately â¹88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel,â he wrote in X post.He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that the NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers.Instead, the Congress leader alleged, the government approved subsidies of more than Rs 4,000 crore for ethanol producers, shifting the benefits of the programme towards industry rather than consumers."E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. World.title: 'No blanket ban on reporting': SC clarifies order restricting use of audio-video clips of court proceedings
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has clarified that its July 24 interim order prohibiting news organisations from sharing or uploading audio and video clips of court hearings does not bar them from reporting on judicial proceedings, but that they cannot use such recordings as part of their reportage.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the restriction is confined to the use of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings in news reports and should not be interpreted as a blanket ban on reportage by media organisations. Such outlets may, therefore, continue to report on the proceedings and inform the general public of legal developments and judicial pronouncements.

"It appears, however, that some confusion persists in respect of paragraph 11 of the earlier order, which this court deems necessary to clarify.

The said paragraph makes it clear that the order is not to be construed as imposing a blanket prohibition on the reporting of court proceedings by recognised news outlets," the bench said in an order on July 31, PTI reported.

However, the news organisations will have to follow the restrictions set out in paragraph 10 of the earlier order.

"In sum, while news outlets may continue to report on the court proceedings, they shall nonetheless remain bound by the restrictions set out in paragraph 10,â the bench added.





The clarification came after Supreme Court noted that "some confusion persists" over the interim order, which barred posting and uploading of audio-video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms without prior permission of the court administration.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âAs an interim measure, it is directed that there shall be no extraction, modification, dissemination, monetisation, posting, reposting and uploading of audio-video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media or other digital platforms without prior permission of the secretary general of this court or the registrar general of the jurisdictional high courts,â the bench had stated in that order.

The Supreme Court had also issued notices to the Centre and others, including some social media platforms, seeking their responses on the plea filed by a journalist.

Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, had described the issue raised in the petition as "very important."

World.title: 'Remake of Dravidian model': Ex-Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin calls Vijay government's budget a 'waste'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK president M K Stalin on Wednesday launched a scathing attack on the TVK government's maiden Budget, calling it a "waste" that merely repackaged schemes introduced during the previous DMK regime while failing to address people's key concerns or fulfil major election promises.

In a post on X shortly after finance minister Marie Wilson presented the 2026-27 Budget in the Assembly, Stalin mocked chief minister C Joseph Vijay, referring to him as the "Reels CM", and said the Budget lacked both originality and vision.

'Expected a blast, got a waste'

"If I had to explain today's TNBudget2026, presented in the Legislative Assembly, in a language that even the 'Reels CM' would understand: People were expecting it to be a 'Blast, Blast' budget, but it has turned out to be more like 'Waste, Waste'!" Stalin said.

He alleged that the Budget was "nothing more than a remake version of the Dravidian Model government's existing schemes" and accused the government of failing to offer any meaningful solutions to pressing public issues.

"In the language of the common people, this is a budget that shows no concern whatsoever for issues such as the problems faced by farmers, the electricity tariff confusion, or the rising cost of living.





Nor does it announce any new long-term visionary plans that the state truly needs," he said.

Stalin further alleged that the government had ignored several major promises made before the Assembly elections, including a monthly financial assistance of Rs 2,500 for women, Rs 4,000 for unemployed youth, six free LPG cylinders every year and a complete waiver of crop loans.

"Overall, this is the first budget of the 'Reels Government'âa budget that shows no original thinking, fails to deliver even on what was promised, lacks substance and vigour and ultimately turns out to be a dull, lacklustre budget," he said.

What the TVK government announced

Earlier in the day, finance minister Marie Wilson presented the TVK government's first Budget, laying out a roadmap to make Tamil Nadu a $1.5 trillion economy by 2031.

The Budget allocated Rs 300 crore for the modernisation of 3,734 government schools and Rs 139 crore for the first phase of the 'Super Clean, Super Campus' initiative in 10,000 schools. It also announced the launch of the 'Vetri Laptop Scheme' for college students and allocated Rs 44,527 crore for the School Education Department and Rs 8,393 crore for Higher Education.

The government also proposed modern residential schools under the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Model Schools scheme, a new law college in Madurai, five new Industrial Training Institutes and a specialised levy on liquor production units expected to generate around Rs 1,000 crore in additional revenue.

The Budget also earmarked more than Rs 1,000 crore for welfare promises, including an eight-gram gold coin and silk saree for eligible brides under the "Annan Seer" scheme, one-gram gold rings for newborns delivered in government hospitals, free milch cows for eligible women and subsidised livestock support for vulnerable groups.

Opposition parties target budget

Along with Stalin's criticism, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami also dismissed the Budget as disappointing, alleging that the TVK government had merely rebranded existing schemes instead of introducing new welfare initiatives.

Palaniswami similarly accused the government of failing to implement major election promises, including enhanced financial assistance for women, six free LPG cylinders and a comprehensive farm loan waiver, while questioning its plan to tackle Tamil Nadu's growing debt burden.

World.title: Kolkata opens its doors after 19 years: Where does Taslima Nasreen go next?
World.content:
For 19 years, Taslima Nasreen carried Kolkata in her memories, longing to return but unable to do so. The city that had become her âsecond homeâ after she left Bangladesh in 1994 remained out of reach.

Forced to flee her country of birth and later compelled to leave the city where she had settled, Nasreen spent much of the past three decades moving from one place to another, not in search of adventure but of refuge, without quite recovering the sense of home she associated with Kolkata.

That door finally opened nearly

r.

Nasreen set foot in the City of Joy on July 31 and received a civic felicitation at Rabindra Sadan on August 1.

The visit was accompanied by a warm official welcome from West Bengalâs new government, with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari assuring the writer of security whenever she chose to visit.

The author, who was forced to leave Kolkata in 2007, responded with gratitude. âItâs not just the city I return to; for me, itâs a homecoming to a lost chapter of my life,â she said.

The change of government has given Nasreen fresh hope of spending more time in Kolkata, something that did not become possible under the previous two administrations. But it has also raised a more difficult question: Is her return merely a ceremonial visit, or could it be the first step towards once again making Kolkata her home?

Homecoming: Delayed, but not denied

In November 2007, Kolkata witnessed violent protests by groups opposed to Nasreen and her writings, including her memoir

Dwikhandito

. Amid concerns over her safety and the worsening law-and-order situation, the authorities moved her out of the city.





She was taken first to Jaipur and later kept under security in New Delhi before eventually leaving India for Europe. Her repeated appeals to successive governments to let her return to Kolkata did not produce a result.

Almost two decades and two changes of government later, her return became possible. âTaslima Nasreenâs return proves that Bengal is in good hands now. Threats and intimidation are in the past. Every pillar of the Constitution and fundamental rights are safe,â Adhikari said at the felicitation.

âYou can come to Kolkata whenever you want, as many times as you want, and

. As the chief minister and police minister of Bengal, I am personally responsible for your security.â Nasreen was equally effusive in her gratitude.

âHistory remembers who shut the door. Now, history will also remember who reopened it,â she said. âThe opening of this door proves injustice can feel like a long night, but itâs never permanent.â But the cordial exchange also opened a larger conversation.

Can Kolkata become a sanctuary to which Nasreen returns not merely as a guest but as a long-term resident? The answer is not straightforward. The chief minister can assure her of security within the state, but any longer-term residential arrangement would also depend on her visa status and decisions by the appropriate immigration authorities. Visa extensions and residential permits for foreign nationals are handled through the FRRO/FRO system and, in some cases, the Union home ministry.

Kolkata: Then and now

Nineteen years is a long time, particularly in a period of rapid political and social change. The Kolkata Nasreen knew in the early 2000s is not the city to which she has returned.

For the writer, âevery year in banishment looked like a door heavily boltedâ. Meanwhile, although the government that moved her out of the city is no longer in power, her return has acquired a new and complicated political context.

Nasreen has not forgotten how abruptly she had to leave Kolkata while the Left Front governed Bengal.

She remains sharply critical of the Left, accusing sections of it of failing to defend free-thinkers while claiming to stand for secularism and progressive values.

But the Kolkata of 2026 is governed by the BJP, and Nasreenâs return unfolded amid the symbols and slogans associated with its politics. Chief Minister Adhikari was welcomed at Rabindra Sadan with chants of âJai Shri Ramâ, a religious invocation that has also become a prominent political slogan.

Nasreen has consistently argued that religion and the state should remain separate.âHumanity has to be bigger than any doctrine,â she said during her homecoming address.

She also sought to draw a clear line between gratitude and political endorsement. âIâm thankful to this government for letting me return. But my gratitude doesnât warrant my allegiance to them. I havenât come here for any political party,â she said.

The question, therefore, is not whether she is grateful to the government that facilitated her return. She plainly is. The harder question is whether Kolkata can protect her right to disagree with the same establishment if her views become inconvenient to it.

The cultural composition of the felicitation offered another indication of how much the cityâs public life has changed. For a ceremony honouring one of the Bengali languageâs most internationally recognised writers, relatively few prominent members of the literary fraternity were present.

Novelist Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay, who had been expected to attend, was absent. Poet Joy Goswami was present, but his appearance led to the most uncomfortable moment of the evening.

When Nasreen invited Goswami to join her on the stage, a section of the audience erupted in protest, shouting slogans and objecting to his presence on the dais. Goswami, who had begun walking towards the stage, turned around and returned to his seat.

The disruption continued for several minutes. Nasreen waited quietly before appealing to the audience to calm down and allow the programme to continue.

The irony was difficult to miss. An event organised to celebrate a writer who had spent decades defending freedom of expression had briefly become a venue for preventing another poet from speaking.

The hostility appeared to be connected to Goswamiâs perceived proximity to the previous Trinamool Congress establishment and criticism that prominent cultural figures had not done enough to defend Nasreen when she was made to leave Kolkata.

Whatever the political grievance, however, it could not justify denying him the opportunity to speak after Nasreen herself had invited him.

Goswami did not confront the protesters and later left Rabindra Sadan without reading the poem he had written for Nasreen.

âEveryone has the right to speak. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it; but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him.

That is not right,â Nasreen said the following day.âIt wasnât just Joy who was insulted. I was also insulted because I had invited him.â

The organisers also expressed regret over the incident. Nasreen subsequently spoke to Goswami by telephone after being unable to visit him during the trip.

The episode showed how quickly cultural spaces can become arenas for political resentment. For all the celebration surrounding Nasreenâs homecoming, Kolkata is still negotiating the same difficult questions about dissent, ideological loyalty and the right to disagree that formed the background to her departure.

The real test will not be how warmly the city welcomes her when her presence suits the political moment. It will be whether Kolkata continues to defend her when she says something those in power, or their supporters, do not wish to hear.

Where to next?

Kolkata has reopened its doors to Nasreen after nearly 19 years. Her own homeland, however, remains out of reach. After

Lajja

provoked widespread outrage among Islamist groups, Nasreen faced threats and criminal proceedings over her writings and public statements.

Her Bangladeshi passport was revoked, and she left the country in 1994.

Nearly 32 years later, she has still not been able to return permanently. Exile remains the defining condition of her life. âThe number of years Iâve been away from home has already surpassed the sum of time I was allowed to live there,â said Nasreen, who will turn 64 later this month.

And yet she has supported former Bangladesh prime minister

s right to return to the country, even though Nasreen has said that Hasinaâs government opposed her own attempts to return to Bangladesh in 1999. âIâve criticised

in the past,â Nasreen said. âThe ban on the Awami League must be revoked since itâs undemocratic.

Sheikh Hasina wants to return. I want her to return for the sake of democracy in Bangladesh.â

Hasina, who has been living in India since her government fell in August 2024, has said she intends to return to Bangladesh by December despite a death sentence handed down in absentia, which she rejects as politically motivated. She was scheduled to make her first public appearance since her ouster through a virtual address in New Delhi on August 5.

Nasreenâs defence of Hasinaâs right to return is notable precisely because of their history. It is an argument that the right to go home should not depend on political sympathy or personal gratitude. âNo one wants my return. Sheikh Hasina did not. Neither did Khaleda Zia nor those who came to power subsequently,â Nasreen said, her disappointment over the repeated refusals unmistakable.

But she refuses to abandon hope. âIt took me 19 years to be able to say, âKolkata, Iâve come back to youâ,â she said.

âI have tears in my eyes, but I come with a heart full of love.â

Her return to the City of Joy has renewed her belief that seemingly permanent barriers can eventually fall. âNineteen years stand between my exile and return. But the opening of this door proves injustice can be long-standing but never permanent.â

Perhaps that is why Nasreen continues to dream of a day âwhen no writer has to live in exile from her own countryâ.

She hopes Bangladesh will one day separate religion from the state and become a country where women have equal rights, minorities can live with dignity and free-thinkers and non-believers are not threatened for their views.

In Indiaâs neighbouring country, that day may yet come. For now, Nasreen is grateful that she can at least return to Kolkata, revisit its familiar spaces and, she hopes, attend the Book Fair as she once did.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Her former address in the city no longer belongs to her. Kolkata has changed, and the pet that once helped make the city feel like home is no longer alive. But after nearly 19 years, Taslima Nasreen has returned, carrying with her hope, unfinished arguments and, perhaps, a few more lives in reserve.

World.title: Lok Sabha secretariat director found hanging in Noida flat; suicide note recovered
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A director in the Lok Sabha Secretariat allegedly died by suicide at his flat in a Noida housing society, police said on Wednesday.

The deceased, identified as Gaurav Gautam, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in his apartment at Kendriya Vihar-II Society in Noida's Sector 82 on Sunday, police said, as cited by PTI.

Police said a purported suicide note recovered from the flat referred to a loan. Its contents are being examined as part of the ongoing investigation.

According to the Phase-2 police station, officers were alerted to the incident after receiving a memo from a hospital, where Gaurav Gautam had been taken. Doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Police said Gautam's wife had gone to her parental home. On returning, she found the flat locked and, sensing that something was wrong, entered the apartment with the assistance of a security guard.

She found Gautam hanging and immediately rushed him to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead, police said.

A forensic team and local police later inspected the scene and collected evidence. After completing the inquest proceedings, the body was sent for a post-mortem examination.

World.title: ‘Vile, abusive’: Bombay HC orders takedown of fake posts targeting Gadkari over E20 ethanol row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday granted interim relief to Union minister

, directing social media intermediaries, including Meta, to take down defamatory deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts linking him and his family to the government's E20 ethanol-blending programme.

The court described the flagged material as âvile and abusiveâ.

Granting interim relief, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed intermediaries, including Meta, to take down deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts falsely linking Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and his family to the E20 fuel controversy, describing the content as "vile and abusive."

The order was passed by Justice Arif Doctor on Wednesday in Gadkari's suit against Meta Platforms, X, Google/YouTube, the Union ministry of electronics and information technology, the department of telecommunications and unidentified users.

The court observed that the material cited by Gadkari was âabsolutely vileâ and abusive, and said such content should not be available on public platforms accessible to young people.

"One such transcript appears on instagram reel. There are other content. The material which plaintiff seeks to pull down, I can only say that the same is absolutely vile abusive. Such material should have no place on public platform, which is accessible to everyone including young," the court said in its interim order, as reported by Bar & Bench.





The court said Gadkari had made out a case for ad interim relief. Meta and Google, which appeared before the court, agreed to remove the material identified in Exhibit C of the plaint. âTheir statement is accepted,â the court said.

The case concerns posts, reels and videos that Gadkari alleged contained manipulated images and videos, including AI-generated âdefamatory contentâ and âdeep fake contentâ. The material allegedly attributed personal responsibility to the Union minister for the E20 programme and suggested that he and his family had derived âundue pecuniary benefitsâ from ethanol blending.

According to the plea, some posts referred to Gadkari's son, Nikhil Gadkari, and his association with CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure Limited, which is involved in manufacturing ethanol and other products. The allegations sought to link that association to purported financial benefits from the E20 programme.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Gadkari has denied the allegations.

The suit also referred to social media content blaming the minister for introducing or mandating E20 petrol and alleging that ethanol-blended fuel had caused damage to vehicles.

Gadkari argued that the posts insinuated corruption, conflict of interest and abuse of office.

The court's interim directions apply to the material identified in the proceedings, rather than constituting a blanket finding on all online criticism of the minister.

The matter will come up for further hearing after four weeks, when the court is expected to consider the case further.

World.title: 'I'm Kalaignar's grandson, M K Stalin's son': Udhayanidhi hits back after release, shares photo
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Senior

leader and Tamil Nadu Leader of the Opposition

on Tuesday hit out at the ruling TVK government after being released from police custody, saying he was not intimidated by his arrest and would continue to fight for farmers and the people.

Sharing a photograph with his father and former chief minister M K Stalin on X, Udhayanidhi invoked his political lineage and accused the government of trying to suppress the opposition.

"I am the grandson of Kalaignar and the son of M K Stalin. I am a cadre of the DMK. We do not fear these tactics. If it means getting arrested while fighting for farmers, not just once - I will get arrested even 100 times. Your repression will never stop our service to the people for even a single day!" he wrote.

'I'm M K Stalin's son': Udhayanidhi shares photo with father after release

Udhayanidhi was briefly arrested on Tuesday morning, a day after his remarks during a protest in Thanjavur over the

with Karnataka sparked a political controversy. During his speech, he was interrupted by chants of "Trisha, Trisha" from the audience. The ruling TVK alleged that his response carried a vulgar double meaning and accused him of lowering the standards of political discourse and insulting the dignity of women.





After being questioned by the police, Udhayanidhi was released later in the day.

Targeting the TVK government after his release, he alleged that the action against him was aimed at diverting attention from farmers' issues.

"The #SofaModel government, which is incapable of wiping away the sorrows of farmers, has arrested me to divert attention from the issues. Using the ruling party's Abusive warriors, they spread defamation against me claiming that I used unnecessary words during the Thanjavur protest.

They registered false cases, thinking they could harass me by dragging me from Chennai to Thanjavur, and tried to satisfy someone," he said.

"Even after arresting me, I looked at the media and said that I view this arrest as a comedy, and only then came along. I did not run away in fear after seeing the police," he added.

Udhayanidhi also referred to the Karur stampede in which 41 people died, accusing the chief minister of avoiding accountability.

"The whole country knows that today's Chief Minister, even when 41 people died in Karur, without meeting their families and without facing the media, fled head over heels in fear that he might be arrested."

"Even after so many lives were lost in Karur - this is the same person who went to Malaysia within the next one month for a film promotion and danced around. The Chief Minister may fear arrest if he wants. I am not afraid of any of that," he said.

"I express my gratitude to the leaders of various political parties, including friendly movements, who condemned my arrest, and to the party comrades across Tamil Nadu who showed unity in support of me," he said.

World.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest updates: T.N. Leader of Opposition says statement wasn't intended as double entendre

Leader of Opposition and DMK youth wing leader Udhayanidhi Stalin, who was arrested and brought to Thanjavur on a complaint alleging he made misogynistic remarks seemingly directed at a film actor, was released on Station Bail on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) night after being subjected to questioning at the Sengipatti Police Station.

Also read | Propriety in public discourse: On Udhayanidhi Stalin’s double entendre remarks

He was questioned for over an hour at the Sengipatti Police Station in connection with the case booked against him on charges of making offensive remarks against a woman actor during the DMK’s demonstration on the Cauvery issue in Thanjavur on Monday (August 3, 2026).

Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin walked out of the station at around 8.15 p.m. to a boisterous welcome from the assembled cadres. He waved to the crowd standing through the car’s sunroof and accepted their greetings.

Ilanthiraiyan directed the police to release Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin today on station bail after questioning. He is being interrogated at Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget: Western districts to gain from textile, tourism, and energy initiatives
World.content:
The western districts of Tamil Nadu, from Coimbatore to Krishnagiri, are expected to benefit from the State Budget 2026-27 announcements on textiles, electricity, and tourism.

Presenting the maiden Budget of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government, the State’s Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson said infrastructure facilities in Tiruppur, a garment-exporting hub, will be upgraded in multiple phases to promote environmentally sustainable textile production. A Tiruppur Textiles Technology Centre (TTTC) will be established with a financial outlay of ₹10 crore for this purpose.

Regarding the energy sector, the Finance Minister said the Coimbatore-Ariyalur 765 kV Transmission Line Project will be implemented through the public-private partnership mode at a cost of ₹4,000 crore. The Phase-II Green Energy Corridor Project, valued at ₹1,187 crore and crucial for evacuating renewable energy from the State’s southern districts, will be expedited alongside the Virudhunagar-Coimbatore 765 kV Transmission Project, valued at ₹1,640 crore, the Minister added.

Further, the State government is pursuing a proposal for a Metro rail line from Hosur in Krishnagiri district to Bommasandra in Karnataka with both the Karnataka government and the Union government.

Addressing the long-pending demand of farmers, he said the government will pursue the implementation of the Anaimalaiyar and Nallar dam projects. Further, the Cauvery river, from Hogenakkal to Srirangam, will be included in a ₹53-crore proposal to promote river tourism across Tamil Nadu.

Announcements for western districts Textile Technology Centre for Tiruppur Comprehensive scheme to mitigate human-wildlife conflict Nambikkai Illam in Salem, among other districts, for people with intellectual disabilities River tourism from Hogenakkal to Srirangam

Tourism promotion

On the tourism front, the State government will launch the Tamil Nadu Eco-Tourism Mission to develop and expand nature-based tourism circuits and destinations, including trekking routes, wildlife safaris, birding and boating trails, eco-friendly stays, and interpretation and visitor centres. The Mission will be implemented across the State’s diverse landscapes, including forests and wildlife areas, through active community participation. This is expected to benefit the western districts.

Mr. Wilson promised a comprehensive human-wildlife conflict mitigation scheme incorporating scientific measures such as hanging solar fences and steel wire rope fencing, community-based forest protection, the appointment of forest protection staff, and GPS-enabled vehicles for conflict management, night patrolling, security, and monitoring across 100 conflict-prone villages in Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Erode, Krishnagiri, the Nilgiris, Salem, Theni, Tirunelveli, Tenkasi, and Tiruppur districts, with an allocation of ₹20 crore for this fiscal.

For the textile sector, the government is looking at a design institute that will be set up with the participation of industry and academia at a cost of ₹60 crore. Technical textiles, an emerging sector, is yet to pick up in the State. The Technical Textiles Transformation Scheme for Entrepreneurs will be implemented in collaboration with international educational and research institutions, with financial assistance from the Tamil Nadu Technical Textiles Mission. This will provide MSMEs and textile manufacturers with international exposure, technical training, technology transfer, market intelligence, innovation support, and business mentorship.

Further, Salem is among the five districts where the Tamil Nadu government will establish an institution for persons with intellectual disabilities under the name ‘Nambikkai Illam’, with a total outlay of ₹4 crore for all five districts. These institutions will provide special education, early intervention services, rehabilitation, and vocational training to children aged three years and above. In the initial stage, each institution will function as a day school with 50 students and will later be upgraded to include residential facilities.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget: Specialised government law college to be set up in Madurai
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government will establish a specialised Government Law College in Madurai offering advanced legal education on a par with a School of Excellence in Law, Finance Minister Marie Wilson said while presenting the Revised Budget in the Legislative Assembly on Wednesday (August 5, 2026).

The college will commence operations in the 2027-28 academic year with an intake of 300 students.

Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates: Finance Minister Marie Wilson announces one-sovereign gold coin for brides in TVK-led govt.’s maiden Budget

The Minister said ₹8,393 crore had been allocated to the Higher Education Department in the Revised Budget Estimates.

NEET abolition

Reiterating Tamil Nadu’s opposition to the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET), the Minister said repeated leaks in the examination at the national level had severely affected the higher education prospects of the next generation. He urged the Union government to immediately abolish the NEET-based admission system and restore medical admissions based on Class XII public examination marks (in Tamil Nadu).

Mr. Wilson also announced the government’s plan to implement the Vetri Laptop Scheme for college students, with an allocation of ₹2,000 crore. The initiative, he said, would equip students with laptops as an essential learning resource.

Improved housing

Emphasising the need to provide decent accommodation for students, the Minister announced the government would establish the Tamil Nadu Student Housing and Infrastructure Corporation (TNSHIC), a dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle, with an initial equity infusion of ₹10 crore.

Under the flagship TN-SUDAR (Tamil Nadu State Upgradation, Development and Advancement of Student Residences) initiative, the government will construct 200 integrated student hostels providing one lakh modern hostel beds across major educational hubs in the State.

The project will be implemented through a de-risked Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer (DBFOT) public-private partnership model, with an estimated capital outlay of ₹3,200 crore.
